cards.front:
When a mother suffers from hyperemesis gravidarum, it is recommended to:

dehydration

The plotted line is within -2z score and +2z score

cards.rationale: Answer: b. The plotted line is moving towards outside the +2z score

cards.back: b. Its purpose is simply to describe behaviors.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Its purpose is simply to describe behaviors.

cards.front:
Examples of qualitative data gathered to understand the nutrition situation in a community: 1. food habits & patterns of people 2. perceptions of mothers on nutrition 3. household with water-sealed toilets 4. leadership structure in the area *
a. 1, 2, 3
b. 2, 3, 4
c. 1, 3, 4
d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
The most important effect of infections on nutritional status: *
a. reduction in the absorption of nutrients such as iron and vitamin A
b. increase in the loss of fluids and nutrients particularly electrolytes
c. increase in nutrient needs due to increased BMR
d. decreased food intake

Studies of populations that provide correlations between dietary habits and disease incidence are called: *
a. epidemiological studies
b. clinical trials
c. descriptive studies
d. historical studies

An experiment wherein the researcher and the subjects do not know who is receiving the treatment or intervention is called: *
a. single blind
b. double blind
c. double control
d. placebo control

The RDA indicates: *
a. the lowest amount of a nutrient that will maintain a specified criterion of adequacy
b. the highest amount of a nutrient that appears safe for most healthy people
c. the average amount of a nutrient that will maintain a specific biochemical or physiological function in half of the people
d. the average amount of a nutrient considered adequate to meet the nutrient needs of practically all healthy people
cards.back: d. the average amount of a nutrient considered adequate to meet the nutrient needs of practically all healthy people
cards.rationale: Answer: d. the average amount of a nutrient considered adequate to meet the nutrient needs of practically all healthy people

cards.front:
A deficiency caused by an inadequate dietary intake is a/an: *
a. overt deficiency
b. covert deficiency
c. primary deficiency
d. secondary deficiency

A successful weight loss depends on: *
a. avoiding fats and limiting water
b. increasing protein and restricting carbohydrate
c. reducing energy intake and increasing physical activity
d. taking supplements and drinking water
cards.back: c. reducing energy intake and increasing physical activity
cards.rationale: Answer: c. reducing energy intake and increasing physical activity

cards.front:
The structure that delivers nutrients to the fetus and returns waste products to the mother: *
a. embryo
b. placenta
c. uterus
d. amniotic sac

To facilitate lactation, a mother would require: *
a. vitamin and mineral supplements
b. a glass of water before each breastfeeding
c. adequate nutrition and rest
d. about 5,000 kcal a day
cards.rationale: Answer: c. adequate nutrition and rest

cards.front:
Dehydration can develop quickly in infants because:
a. they lose a lot of water through urination and tears.
b. only a small percentage of their body weight is water.
c. much of their body water is extracellular.
d. they consume a lot of breast milk or formula, but little water
cards.back: c. much of their body water is extracellular.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. much of their body water is extracellular.

cards.front:
This program was launched in 1989 to reduce poverty and malnutrition in depressed areas of the country. *
a. FIDEL
b. SPM
c. LAKASS
d. BIDANI

If an elderly drinks too much coffee or tea: *
a. there should be an increased intake of carbohydrate
b. there would be frequent urination
c. there would be an increased need for thiamin
d. there would be a decreased intake of water
cards.back: c. there would be an increased need for thiamin
cards.rationale: Answer: c. there would be an increased need for thiamin

cards.front:
The agency that assists in the establishment of functional nutrition committees in every region, province, city, municipality, and barangay is: *
a. DA
b. DSWD
c. DOH
d. DILG

Municipal nutrition programs are formulated to: *
a. identify targets
b. select appropriate programs/projects
c. minimize overlaps
d. none of the above

Sole reliance on breast milk for infants beyond 6 months leads to: *
a. xerophthalmia
b. anemia
c. vitamin B deficiency
d. zinc deficiency

Beikost is: *
a. food other than milk
b. milk other than breast milk
c. breast milk from wet nurse
d. soy-based formula
cards.rationale: Answer: a. food other than milk

cards.front:
Ascaris lumbricoides interferes with the absorption of: *
a. fat & Ca
b. Fe & fat
c. Fe & Zn
d. Ca & Fe

Nutrients linked with appetite: *
a. thiamin & leucine
b. thiamin & zinc
c. leucine & zinc
d. leucine & iron

A public health nutritionist is an assessor of people’s nutrition problems if he/she: *
a. finds out the nutrition problems of the community
b. assists the people in solving the nutrition problems
c. initiates the organization of the community in solving the identified nutrition problems
d. plans and evaluates nutrition education programs
cards.back: a. finds out the nutrition problems of the community
cards.rationale: Answer: a. finds out the nutrition problems of the community

cards.front:
A public health nutritionist needs to have knowledge of: *
a. nutrient composition of foods
b. principles of management
c. both a & b
d. a only

As a community organizer, a public health nutritionist engages in:
a. helping people to alleviate their problems
b. supervising field personnel
c. discovering potential leaders in the community
d. identifying the nutritional problems in the community
cards.back: c. discovering potential leaders in the community
cards.rationale: Answer: c. discovering potential leaders in the community

cards.front:
Planning programs/projects/activities that will involve local leaders, the implementors, and the people themselves is known as: *
a. participatory planning
b. local level planning
c. development planning
d. program planning

Management skill/s needed by a public health nutritionist is/are: *
a. interpersonal relations
b. decision making
c. use of statistics
d. all of the above

An important enabling mechanism of the PPAN which convinces and mobilizes influential individuals to participate actively in PPAN implementation: *
a. Nutrition promotion
b. Policy formulation
c. Research
d. Advocacy

The country’s emergency and disaster feeding program is handled by: *
a. DA
b. DOH
c. DSWD
d. DILG

It is included in the rice exchange list except: *
a. chestnut
b. regular ice cream
c. cassava cake
d. soy bean

The agency which pioneered the organization of nutrition councils now known as nutrition committees in the regional, provincial, municipal, and barangay levels: *
a. NCP
b. NFP
c. NNC
d. DILG

Behavior change in the individual occurs in stages. The first stage involves: *
a. acquiring information
b. awareness of the need for change
c. desire to change behavior
d. none of the above
cards.back: b. awareness of the need for change
cards.rationale: Answer: b. awareness of the need for change

cards.front:
The level of this nutrient in breastmilk is maintained at the expense of the mother if her intake is inadequate: *
a. Na
b. Ca
c. Fe
d. P

The major implementor of food labeling regulations in the country: *
a. FDA
b. DOH
c. FNRI
d. DOST

Ingredients are listed in food labels according to: *
a. ascending order of predominance by weight
b. descending order of predominance by weight
c. alphabetical order
d. the manufacturer’s order of preference
cards.back: b. descending order of predominance by weight
cards.rationale: Answer: b. descending order of predominance by weight

cards.front:
On the average, an adult’s energy needs: *
a. decline 5% per year
b. decline 5% per decade
c. remain stable throughout life
d. decline gradually throughout life

A dietary assessment method that can be used to conduct a kilocalorie count: *
a. direct observation
b. food frequency questionnaire
c. 24-hour food recall interview
d. food record

A sign of PEM that will not likely be observed in a physical examination: *
a. dull, brittle hair
b. low serum protein levels
c. poor wound healing
d. wasting
cards.rationale: Answer: b. low serum protein levels

cards.front:
Which of the following is not a sign of dehydration? *
a. sunken eyes
b. reduced urinary output
c. loss of skin turgor
d. edema

If you have a limited budget and time to do a household food consumption survey, what is the best alternative dietary method to use? *
a. food frequency
b. food record
c. family food account
d. food list

Which statement is not correct? *
a. Fat-free does not mean calorie-free,
b. Avocados and olives contain only traces of fat.
c. A small amount of certain types of fat in the diet is needed by the body.
d. Fruits and vegetables are essentially fat-free.
cards.back: b. Avocados and olives contain only traces of fat.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Avocados and olives contain only traces of fat.

cards.front:
Joseph eats the following foods from the Rice Exchange List: 1 cup boiled rice 1 cup pasta 6 pieces of pan de sal (5x5 cm) ½ cup oatmeal The total number of exchanges consumed by Joseph for the day is: *
a. 10
b. 8
c. 6
d. 4

Nutrition education can do the following except: *
a. increase a client’s awareness of nutrition issues
b. compensate for the lack of nutrition services
c. demonstrate or illustrate certain skills
d. change attitudes to create support for individual or collective action
cards.back: b. compensate for the lack of nutrition services
cards.rationale: Answer: b. compensate for the lack of nutrition services

decks.title: CPHN+ :: CHNI - Mockboards3 Community and Applied Nutrition
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (CPHN+ :: CHNI - Mockboards3 Community and Applied Nutrition).

cards.front:
These are the characteristics of a Food Frequency Questionnaire: *
a. It is fast to administer, has low respondent burden, and a high response rate but accuracy is low.
b. It is labor intensive, time-consuming, and results depend on the skill of the interviewer.
c. It is accurate but time-consuming and expensive.
d. It is expensive, easy to administer, and has low respondent burden so that compliance is high.
cards.back: a. It is fast to administer, has low respondent burden, and a high response rate but accuracy is low.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. It is fast to administer, has low respondent burden, and a high response rate but accuracy is low.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements is true about vital health statistics? *
a. It identifies individuals or groups who are malnourished in a community.
b. It provides qualitative and quantitative information.
c. The age specific mortality of 1-4 years is a useful indicator of a community’s nutritional status.
d. Vital health statistics provide very accurate data.
cards.back: c. The age specific mortality of 1-4 years is a useful indicator of a community’s nutritional status.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. The age specific mortality of 1-4 years is a useful indicator of a community’s nutritional status.

cards.front:
Developing a causal model is useful in nutrition assessment. It includes programs that will solve the identified nutrition problem *
a. Only the second statement is correct.
b. Both statements are correct.
c. Only the first statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: c. Only the first statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Only the first statement is correct.

cards.front:
Family food account consists of a daily record of all foods entering the household which is prepared by the household head for a specific period of time. When using a Family Food Record, the food intake of the individual can be estimated using assignment factor or weighting, according to sex and age. *
a. Both statements are correct.
b. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

cards.front:
In developing a Food Frequency Questionnaire, a 24-hour recall is needed. In a qualitative FFQ, portion size estimates are included. *
a. Both statements are correct.
b. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: b. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
cards.rationale:
Answer:
b. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

cards.front:
A program objective is stated in the same way as a research objective. “To decrease the prevalence of severe malnutrition among preschoolers by 80% within a 2- year period” is an example of a program objective. *
a. Both statements are correct.
b. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

cards.front:
It is known as the obesity index. *
a. weight-height ration
b. waist circumference
c. BMI
d. none of the above

Compulsive eating of cornstarch or laundry starch. *
a. geophagia
b. pagophagia
c. amylophagia
d. none of the above

Examples of interpersonal channels of communication except: *
a. workshops
b. facilitated group discussion
c. patient counseling
d. community meetings
cards.rationale: Answer: d. community meetings

cards.front:
The composition of human milk changes: *
a. over the time of day, but stays constant through a single feeding, and over time from birth.
b. over the time from birth, but stays constant through a single feeding and over the day.
c. over a single feeding and across the day, but stays constant over time from birth.
d. over the time of day, within a single feeding, and over the time since birth.
cards.back: d. over the time of day, within a single feeding, and over the time since birth.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. over the time of day, within a single feeding, and over the time since birth.

cards.front:
Constipation during pregnancy is due to: *
a. excessive hormone secretion by the placenta
b. increased plasma volume
c. increased gastric and intestinal transit time
d. decreased motility of the GIT
cards.back: d. decreased motility of the GIT
cards.rationale: Answer: d. decreased motility of the GIT

cards.front:
The UNICEF framework considers the following as underlying causes of malnutrition: 1. inadequate food intake 3. Inadequate care given to children & women 2. unhealthy environment 4. Insufficient health services *
a. 1 & 2
b. 2 & 3
c. 1 & 3
d. 1 & 4

The UNICEF framework considers the following as underlying causes of malnutrition: 1. inadequate food intake 3. Inadequate care given to children & women 2. inadequate access to food in a household 4. Frequently having diseases & illnesses *
a. 1 & 4
b. 2 & 3
c. 1 & 2
d. 1 & 3

The term “fat-free” in food labels means: *
a. 3 grams or less fat per serving
b. less than 1 gram of fat per serving
c. less than 0.5 grams of fat per serving
d. 2 grams or less fat per serving
cards.back: c. less than 0.5 grams of fat per serving
cards.rationale: Answer: c. less than 0.5 grams of fat per serving

cards.front:
A sodium-free and salt-free food product contains: *
a. less than 2mg of Na per serving
b. less than 3mg of Na per serving
c. less than 4mg of Na per serving
d. less than 5mg of Na per serving
cards.back: d. less than 5mg of Na per serving
cards.rationale: Answer: d. less than 5mg of Na per serving

cards.front:
A “low-kcalorie” food product contains: *
a. ≤ 5kcals per serving
b. ≤ 10kcals per serving
c. ≤ 20 kcals per serving
d. ≤ 40 kcals per serving
cards.back: d. ≤ 40 kcals per serving
cards.rationale: Answer: d. ≤ 40 kcals per serving

cards.front:
Very frequent symptoms of iron deficiency anemia, except: *
a. fatigue
b. headache
c. dyspnea
d. koilonychia

The initial stage of iron deficiency anemia can be detected by: *
a. a low transferrin saturation level
b. a low serum ferritin level
c. hemoglobin production falls
d. a high level of erythrocyte protoporphyrin
cards.back: b. a low serum ferritin level
cards.rationale: Answer: b. a low serum ferritin level

cards.front:
A measurement of body stores of vitamin A indicating either a deficiency or excessive status: *
a. retinol binding protein
b. serum retinol
c. urinary excretion of vitamin A
d. none of the above

A sample of 1000 people includes 120 who are hearing-impaired and 50 who are diabetic. If the number who are both diabetic and hearing-impaired is 6, which of the following is true? *
a. Diabetes and hearing impairment appear to be independent characteristics.
b. Diabetics appear to be protected from hearing impairment.
c. Diabetics appear to be at greater risk of hearing impairment.
d. There is an interaction between diabetes and hearing impairment.
cards.back: a. Diabetes and hearing impairment appear to be independent characteristics.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Diabetes and hearing impairment appear to be independent characteristics.

cards.front:
Correct statements concerning dietary iron and anemia include all of the following except: *
a. Serum ferritin and transferrin saturation should be obtained when performing primary screening for IDA.
b. Hemoglobin levels below those considered normal for pregnancy have been associated with infants of low birth weight.
c. Iron deficiency anemia occurs most frequently in young children, women of reproductive age, and the elderly.
d. Iron-rich foods include lean meats and whole grain products.
cards.back: a. Serum ferritin and transferrin saturation should be obtained when performing primary screening for IDA.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Serum ferritin and transferrin saturation should be obtained when performing primary screening for IDA.

cards.front:
The major environmental source of lead absorbed in the human blood stream in adults is: *
a. air
b. water
c. lead-based paint
d. food

A woman’s need for _____ is greater during lactation than during pregnancy. *
a. vitamin D
b. energy
c. calcium
d. folate

Ascaris lumbricoides interferes with the absorption of: *
a. fat & calcium
b. iron & fat
c. iron & zinc
d. calcium & iron

For malnourished and underweight people, protein and energy-dense snacks include: *
a. whole grains & high-fiber legumes
b. yogurt & cottage cheese
c. hard boiled eggs and peanut butter & crackers
d. fresh fruits and vegetables
cards.back: c. hard boiled eggs and peanut butter & crackers
cards.rationale: Answer: c. hard boiled eggs and peanut butter & crackers

cards.front:
An effective communication technique to use while interviewing a client is to: *
a. give the client advice when he describes his eating habits
b. ask close-ended questions so that the client will not have to think too hard
c. let the client do most of the talking
d. use and follow a guide for asking important questions
cards.back: c. let the client do most of the talking
cards.rationale: Answer: c. let the client do most of the talking

cards.front:
Factors such as a person’s age, education, and ethnic identity are part of the _____ history. *
a. socio-economic
b. health
c. diet
d. ecological

An advantage of food intake records is that: *
a. The client may change eating behaviors during the times records are kept.
b. The client may also record behaviors associated with eating symptoms, associated with eating foods, and physical activities.
c. The client must diligently maintain the record.
d. The records are easy to keep.
cards.back: b. The client may also record behaviors associated with eating symptoms, associated with eating foods, and physical activities.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. The client may also record behaviors associated with eating symptoms, associated with eating foods, and physical activities.

cards.front:
All of the following are true about physical findings used in nutrition assessments except: *
a. physical findings are highly specific
b. physical findings help confirm suspected nutrient deficiencies
c. physical findings can help detect dehydration and fluid retention
d. physical findings can reflect both nutrient imbalances and conditions unrelated to nutrition
cards.back: a. physical findings are highly specific
cards.rationale: Answer: a. physical findings are highly specific

cards.front:
A child 2 years of age should eat: *
a. at least 3 times a day
b. 4 -5 times a day
c. twice a day
d. 5 – 6 times a day
cards.back: d. 5 – 6 times a day
cards.rationale: Answer: d. 5 – 6 times a day

cards.front:
It is the most reliable method to diagnose anemia and identify the cause: *
a. clinical examination
b. dietary assessment
c. laboratory test
d. none of the above

The only way to treat severely anemic individuals particularly pregnant women is: *
a. supplementation
b. food fortification
c. nutrition education
d. deworming

All are vitamin A-rich foods except: *
a. alugbati
b. tiesa
c. malunggay leaves
d. ampalaya fruit

A pregnant woman should not take supplements of: *
a a. Fe
b. vitamin A
c. folate
d. vitamin C

A woman needs iron supplements during lactation: *
a. to enhance the iron in her breast milk
b. to replace her body’s iron stores
c. to provide iron for the infant’s growth
d. to support the increase in her blood volume
cards.back: b. to replace her body’s iron stores
cards.rationale: Answer: b. to replace her body’s iron stores

cards.front:
Nutrients that seem to protect against cataract development among older adults: *
a. lecithin
b. minerals
c. antioxidants
d. amino acids

The % usual body weight of a person who weighs 135 lbs. and has a usual body weight of 150 lbs. is: *
a. 74%
b. 86%
c. 90%
d. 101%

A malnourished acutely ill patient has just begun to eat after days without significant amounts of food. The test result that would change most quickly as the patient’s health and nutrition status improves is: *
a. transferrin
b. albumin
c. serum electrolytes
d. retinol binding protein

A successful nutrition counseling would include a long list of: *
a. appetizing meals and foods that the patient can include in the diet
b. foods that the patient should avoid
c. dietary changes that the patient should consider making
d. reasons why the patient should make dietary changes
cards.back: b. foods that the patient should avoid
cards.rationale: Answer: b. foods that the patient should avoid

cards.front:
An important factor that would affect how nutrition education should be presented is: *
a. the person’s medical history
b. the person’s nutrient needs and nutritional status
c. the person’s abilities and motivations
d. the entries in the patient’s medical record
cards.back: c. the person’s abilities and motivations
cards.rationale: Answer: c. the person’s abilities and motivations

cards.front:
Community participation can lead to community empowerment and self-reliance. It can result in better program/project implementation. *
a. Both statements are incorrect.
b. Both statements are correct.
c. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
d. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Both statements are correct.

cards.front:
The reason why male teenagers have higher allowance for iodine than female teenagers is: *
a. they have higher energy needs
b. they have more muscles
c. they have higher basal metabolism
d. they have higher protein needs
cards.back: a. they have higher energy needs
cards.rationale: Answer: a. they have higher energy needs

cards.front:
Which of the following statements is true? *
a. Elderly males are less prone to develop IDA.
b. Elderly men are likely to be overweight.
c. Elderly women are two times more likely to be overweight.
d. Elderly females are more prone to develop IDA.
cards.back: c. Elderly women are two times more likely to be overweight.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Elderly women are two times more likely to be overweight.

cards.front:
Using the lecture method ensures good audience participation. It is a method that allows the teacher to give more information in a short period of time. *
a. Both statements are incorrect.
b. Only the first statement is correct.
c. Both statements are incorrect.
d. Only the second statement is correct.
cards.back: d. Only the second statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Only the second statement is correct.

cards.front:
VAD is a major cause of blindness. It is associated with low mortality among children. *
a. Both statements are incorrect.
b. Both statements are correct.
c. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
d. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
cards.back: d. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

cards.front:
The best advice to give to a mother of a marasmic child to improve her child’s condition is: *
a. Give the child vitamin and mineral supplements.
b. Add animal foods such as chicken, pork, fish to the child’s diet.
c. Increase the rice consumption of the child.
d. Give the child more fruits and vegetables.
cards.back: b. Add animal foods such as chicken, pork, fish to the child’s diet.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Add animal foods such as chicken, pork, fish to the child’s diet.

cards.front:
Nutrition rehabilitation is a developmental intervention. It will develop the mental capacity of a malnourished child. *
a. Both statements are correct.
b. Only the second statement is correct.
c. Only the first statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Both statements are incorrect.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements is not true? *
a. Fiber and “roughage” mean the same thing.
b. Meat contains essentially no carbohydrates.
c. Milk is rich in iron while egg is high in calcium.
d. No single food contains all the nutrients needed to maintain good health.
cards.back: c. Milk is rich in iron while egg is high in calcium.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Milk is rich in iron while egg is high in calcium.

cards.front:
The reason for conducting a program planning is ____: *
a. to guide all actions to a common goal.
b. to experience the process involved in planning a program.
c. to inform others of what is being done.
d. to follow the set requirement of the funding agency.
cards.back: a. to guide all actions to a common goal.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. to guide all actions to a common goal.

cards.front:
What is the iron content of 1 cup of boiled rice? Given: 1 cup = 240g; FCT value for well-milled boiled rice: 100% EP is 11mg calcium; 0.6mg iron. *
a. 1.0mg
b. 0.9mg
c. 0.96mg
d. 1.44mg

What information is needed to develop a weight gain plan for newly pregnant women? *
a. physical activity
b. number of previous pregnancies
c. weight and height
d. income level

The best definition of a community is: *
a. Its residents belong to an ethnic group.
b. A group of people with common characteristics.
c. A group of people living within a territorial boundary.
d. It refers to a barangay.
cards.back: b. A group of people with common characteristics.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. A group of people with common characteristics.

cards.front:
The best strategy to make participants acquire skills in problem identification and decision-making is: *
a. Let the participants read the handouts before the lecture.
b. Use the lecture-discussion only.
c. Start with a brief lecture followed by role playing.
d. Use the demonstration method.
cards.back: c. Start with a brief lecture followed by role playing.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Start with a brief lecture followed by role playing.

cards.front:
The food consumption method that asks respondents how often they eat a certain food is: *
a. food inventory
b. food frequency
c. food recall
d. food record

Radio and television are popular channels for nutrition education. Both can reach large and small audiences. *
a. The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
b. Both statements are incorrect.
c. Both statements are correct.
d. The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Both statements are correct.

cards.front:
Which of the following communication channels allows the participants to apply new knowledge and skills? *
a. video tapes
b. case studies
c. lectures
d. panel discussions

Breast milk does not contain casein unlike cow’s milk. Its protein content is slightly higher than cow’s milk. *
a. Only the first statement is correct.
b. Both statements are correct.
c. Only the second statement is correct.
d. Both statements are incorrect.
cards.back: a. Only the first statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Only the first statement is correct.

cards.front:
The simplest biochemical method used to detect iodine deficiency: *
a. serum thyroxine
b. protein bound iodine
c. urinary iodine excretion
d. radioactive iodine uptake

Certain population groups are nutritionally at-risk. Nutrition programs should therefore be need- oriented. *
a. Only the first statement is correct.
b. Both statements are incorrect.
c. Both statements are correct.
d. Only the second statement is correct.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Both statements are correct.

cards.front:
The first law passed to regulate the practice of dietetics in the Philippines: *
a. Science Act of the Philippines
b. Dietetic Law of the Philippines
c. Nutrition Act of the Philippines
d. Nutrition and Dietetics Decree
cards.back: b. Dietetic Law of the Philippines
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Dietetic Law of the Philippines

cards.front:
What food combinations would be the best sources of complete protein? *
a. cereal and grains
b. peanut and kidney beans
c. gelatin and whipped cream
d. milk and eggs

a. Conducting a pre-post knowledge test for all program participants to measure educational outcomes
b. Implementing a randomized trial to compare the new program's outcomes against a standard intervention
c. Establishing a continuous improvement (CQI) process that involves regular feedback loops from stakeholders and data-driven adjustments to program activities
d. Performing an annual peer review of all materials and educational handouts to ensure scientific accuracy
cards.back: c. Establishing a continuous improvement (CQI) process that involves regular feedback loops from stakeholders and data-driven adjustments to program activities
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Establishing a continuous improvement (CQI) process that involves regular feedback loops from stakeholders and data-driven adjustments to program activities
options: Conducting a pre-post knowledge test for all program participants to measure educational outcomes
Implementing a randomized trial to compare the new program's outcomes against a standard intervention
Establishing a continuous improvement (CQI) process that involves regular feedback loops from stakeholders and data-driven adjustments to program activities
Performing an annual peer review of all materials and educational handouts to ensure scientific accuracy

decks.title: FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON BASIC NUTRITION
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON BASIC NUTRITION).

cards.front:
What would be the appropriate weight gain of a person who consumes an excess of 500kcal daily for a month?*
a. 0.5 lb
b. 2 lbs
c. 3 lbs
d. 4 lbs

What is considered to be a healthy rate of weight loss for most overweight people on a long-term basis?*
a. 0.5-1 lb/week
b. 2-3 lbs/week
c. 4-5 lbs/week
d. 7-8 lbs/week

Which of the following describes the process of thermogenesis?*
a. Burning of fat
b. Synthesis of fat
c. Generation of heat
d. Generation of water

Which of the following is a feature of the basal metabolic rate?*
a. Fever decreases BMR
b. Fasting increases BMR
c. Pregnancy increases BMR
d. Females have higher BMR than males

If a dancer and a typist are the same height and have the exact same body build, the dancer will be heavier because she has*
a. more body fat
b. stronger bones
c. stronger muscles
d. more muscle mass

What is the approximate value for the thermic effect of a 2,500 kcal diet?*
a. 25 kcal
b. 250 kcal
c. 400 kcal
d. 500 kcal

What is the approximate basal metabolism of a 110 lb woman?*
a. 850 kcal/day
b. 960kcal/day
c. 1080 kcal/day
d. 1240 kcal/day

Which of the following is a feature of the BMI?*
a. It correlates with disease risks.
b. It decreases by 1 unit for every 10 years of life.
c. It provides an estimate of the fat level of the body.
d. It is defined as the person’s height divided by the square of the weight.
cards.back: a. It correlates with disease risks.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. It correlates with disease risks.

cards.front:
Which of the following is a feature of fatfold assessment techniques?*
a. The device to measure fatfold thickness is called a lipidmeter.
b. The folds of fat increase in size proportion to the gain in body fat.
c. Measures taken from upper-body sites are more precise than those from lower-body sites
d. The principles are based on the assumption that subcutaneous fat mass represents about 20% of total body fat.
cards.back: b. The folds of fat increase in size proportion to the gain in body fat.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. The folds of fat increase in size proportion to the gain in body fat.

cards.front:
Which of the following is a feature of the waist-to-hip ratio indicator?*
a. It correlates very closely to underwater weighing.
b. It is most useful in accessing changes in body fat.
c. It is calculated by dividing the waist circumference by the square of the hip dimension.
d. It generally remains constant despite weight loss-induced changes in body fat distribution
cards.back: b. It is most useful in accessing changes in body fat.
cards.rationale:
Answer:
b. It is most useful in accessing changes in body fat.

cards.front:
General characteristics of water-soluble vitamins include all of the following except*
a. They must be consumed daily.
b. Toxic levels in the body are rarely found.
c. They are absorbed directly into the blood.
d. Excesses are eliminated from the kidneys.
cards.back: a. They must be consumed daily.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. They must be consumed daily.

cards.front:
Which of the following vitamins would be removed in the production of skim milk?*
a. Thiamin
b. Vitamin A
c. Riboflavin
d. Vitamin B12

Which of the following is not a general characteristic of the fat-soluble vitamin?*
a. Excesses are eliminated from the kidneys.
b. Absorption is via the lymphatic circulation.
c. Several of them require protein carriers for transport.
d. They can be stored in relatively large amounts in certain body tissues.
cards.back: a. Excesses are eliminated from the kidneys.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Excesses are eliminated from the kidneys.

cards.front:
Which of the following explains why B vitamins deficiencies lead to lack of energy?*
a. B vitamins are a source of kcalories.
b. Absorption of carbohydrates and fats is decreased.
c. Oxygen for energy metabolism cannot be transported to the cells.
d. Coenzymes needed for energy metabolism are produced in insufficient amounts.
cards.back: d. Coenzymes needed for energy metabolism are produced in insufficient amounts.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Coenzymes needed for energy metabolism are produced in insufficient amounts.

cards.front:
Which of the following diets is likely to lead to beriberi?*
a. Low intakes of whole grains
b. High intakes of polished rice
c. High intakes of unrefined rice
d. Low intakes of enriched grains
cards.back: b. High intakes of polished rice
cards.rationale: Answer: b. High intakes of polished rice

cards.front:
Which of the following is a characteristic of thiamin stability in relation to cooking method?*
a. Microwaving the food conserves much of the thiamin.
b. Prolonged heating of the food has little, if any, affect on the vitamin.
c. Boiling the food tends to conserve thiamin by a forming stable, hydrated complex.
d. Steaming the food can lead to substantial thiamin loss due to high heat needed to form the steam.
cards.back: d. Steaming the food can lead to substantial thiamin loss due to high heat needed to form the steam.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Steaming the food can lead to substantial thiamin loss due to high heat needed to form the steam.

cards.front:
If one identical twin who leads a sedentary lifestyle has a RENI of 1.3mg of B2, what would be the approximate recommendation for the other twin who engages in regular physical activity?*
a. 1.3mg
b. 1.6mg
c. 1.9mg
d. 2.6mg

What is the function of intrinsic factor in vitamin B12 absorption?*
a. It catalyzes release of the vitamin from its protein-bound form.
b. It attaches to the vitamin thereby allowing absorption of the vitamin.
c. It acts as a storage protein for the vitamin within the intestinal epithelial cells.
d. It acts as a cofactor for mucosal enzymes involved in absorption of the vitamin
cards.back: b. It attaches to the vitamin thereby allowing absorption of the vitamin.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. It attaches to the vitamin thereby allowing absorption of the vitamin.

cards.front:
What is the most common treatment for pernicious anemia?*
a. Injection of cobalamin
b. Topical administration of liver extract
c. Oral supplements of B-complex vitamins
d. A diet high in green leafy vegetables
cards.back: c. Oral supplements of B-complex vitamins
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Oral supplements of B-complex vitamins

cards.front:
Which of the following is known to perform an essential function in the human body?*
a. Inositol
b. Ubiquinone
c. Pangamic acid
d. PABA

What is the minimum amount of ascorbic acid that will prevent scurvy in human beings?*
a. 10 mg
b. 30mg
c. 50mg
d. 60mg

Which of these meals is lacking in vitamin C?*
a. Hamburger, boiled baby carrots and corn, noodles, and tea
b. Hotdog, coleslaw, French fries, milk
c. Grilled chicken, rice, broccoli, coffee
d. Spaghetti with meat sauce in tomatoes, garlic bread, Coke
cards.back: a. Hamburger, boiled baby carrots and corn, noodles, and tea
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Hamburger, boiled baby carrots and corn, noodles, and tea

cards.front:
Which of the following food groups contains the highest amount of vitamins when expressed per kcal?*
a. dairy
b. meats
c. fruits
d. vegetables

Which of the following features do vitamins C and E share?*
a. Both function as antioxidants.
b. Both require bile for absorption.
c. Neither participates in protein synthesis
d. Neither is affected by the processing of foods
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Both function as antioxidants.

cards.front:
All of the following are properties of electrolytes except*
a. They attract water.
b. They are charged particles.
c. They carry electrical current.
d. They include fat-soluble as well as water-soluble particles.
cards.back: d. They include fat-soluble as well as water-soluble particles.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. They include fat-soluble as well as water-soluble particles.

cards.front:
Which of the following describes a way to make an electrolyte solution?*
a. Dissolve a teaspoon of salt in a glass of water.
b. Vigorously shake a mixture of corn oil and water.
c. Dissolve a pinch of cornstarch in a glass of water.
d. Vigorously shake a pinch of table sugar in warm water.
cards.back: a. Dissolve a teaspoon of salt in a glass of water.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Dissolve a teaspoon of salt in a glass of water.

cards.front:
When a person loses fluid by sweating or bleeding, what minerals are lost in greatest quantity?*
a. Sodium and chloride
b. Bicarbonate and sulfate
c. Calcium and magnesium
d. Potassium and phosphate

In a normal individual with a daily requirement of 500 mg sodium, what would be the sodium balance afteran intake of 10g of table salt contain 4000 mg NA?*
a. Equilibrium
b. Slight positive balance
c. Strong positive balance
d. Moderate positive balance

How much sodium is contained in a fast food deluxe hamburger that lists a salt content of 5g of salt contains 2,300mg NA?*
a. 100 mg
b. 125 mg
c. 1,000 mg
d. 2,500 mg

All of the following are features of potassium in nutrition except*
a. Processed foods are a major source
b. High intakes may protect against stroke
c. Per serving size, legumes are a rich source
d. Per serving size, bananas are good sources
cards.back: a. Processed foods are a major source
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Processed foods are a major source

cards.front:
Which of the following is not a process that directly involves calcium?*
a. pH regulation
b. blood clotting
c. nerve transmission
d. maintenance of heart beat

All of the following characteristics are shared by calcium and magnesium except*
a. Both are involved in blood clotting.
b. Both are involved in bone formation.
c. Both are found in abundance in dairy products.
d. Both may result in tetany when blood levels become abnormally low.
cards.back: a. Both are involved in blood clotting.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Both are involved in blood clotting.

cards.front:
How much calcium a normal adult with a calcium intake of 1,000 mg would typically absorb?*
a. 100 mg
b. 300 mg
c. 600 mg
d. 950 mg

Which of the following individuals would most likely need an iron supplement?*
a. a 1-year old child
b. Elderly female
c. Pregnant female
d. Adolescent female

Which of the following is the most effective and least costly strategy for preventing an iron deficiency?*
a. Consume iron supplements at a level 2-3 times the RENI.
b. Switch to iron cooking utensils and eat at least 4 servings of red meat daily.
c. Eat small amounts of citrus products and increase intake of low-fat milk.
d. Eat small quantities of meat, fish, and poultry frequently together with liberal amounts of vegetables and legumes.
cards.back: d. Eat small quantities of meat, fish, and poultry frequently together with liberal amounts of vegetables and legumes.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Eat small quantities of meat, fish, and poultry frequently together with liberal amounts of vegetables and legumes.

cards.front:
Zinc is known to play an important role in all of the following functions except*
a. Wound healing
b. Synthesis of retinal
c. Production of sperm
d. Oxidation of PUFAs

Which of the following would be the most appropriate food source of iodine for a person who lives inland?*
a. Fresh water fish
b. Iodized salt
c. Locally grown produce
d. Plants of the cabbage family

Which of the following nutrients has functions similar to those of vitamin E?*
a. Iron
b. Selenium
c. Chromium
d. Molybdenum

Which of the following characteristics do copper and fluoride share?*
a. Both may be obtained from drinking tap water.
b. Both serve as cofactor for a number of enzymes.
c. Neither is involved in the integrity of bones and teeth.
d. Neither is known to be toxic at intakes of 10 times the estimated safe intake.
cards.back: a. Both may be obtained from drinking tap water.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Both may be obtained from drinking tap water.

cards.front:
Characteristics of manganese in nutrition include all of the following except*
a. Good sources are plant sources
b. Deficiencies are seen primarily in the elderly
c. Absorption is inhibited by calcium supplements
d. Toxicity is more common from environmental contamination than from the diet
cards.back: b. Deficiencies are seen primarily in the elderly
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Deficiencies are seen primarily in the elderly

cards.front:
Among the following minerals, which may be found in very minute amount in food and water?*
a. Lead
b. Boron
c. Silver
d. Cadmium

Which of the following is a poor source of potassium?*
a. Banana
b. Potato
c. Lettuce
d. Melon

Athletes can safely add muscle tissue by*
a. increasing protein intake
b. taking ergogenic aids
c. putting a demand on the muscles by making them work harder
d. increasing protein intake while decreasing CHO intake
cards.back: c. putting a demand on the muscles by making them work harder
cards.rationale: Answer: c. putting a demand on the muscles by making them work harder

cards.front:
In weight training, muscle strength can best be emphasized by combining a*
a. low number of repetitions with heavy weights
b. low number of repetitions with light weights
c. high number of repetitions with heavy weights
d. high number of repetitions with light weights
cards.back: a. low number of repetitions with heavy weights
cards.rationale: Answer: a. low number of repetitions with heavy weights

cards.front:
What is VO2 max?*
a. An individual’s maximum velocity on a test treadmill.
b. An individual’s maximum rate of oxygen consumption.
c. An individual’s maximum oxygen uptake on rest.
d. An individual’s maximum intake of air at 70% exhaustion.
cards.back: b. An individual’s maximum rate of oxygen consumption.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. An individual’s maximum rate of oxygen consumption.

cards.front:
What is the predominant fuel used by muscle cells during low intensity activity?*
a. Fat
b. amino acids
c. glycogen
d. blood glucose

Which of the following activities may lead to a fast depletion of glycogen?*
a. Hiking
b. Jogging
c. Walking
d. Quarter kilometer run

Which of the following is a common product of anaerobic metabolism?*
a. lactic acid
b. phytic acid
c. phosphoric acid
d. phosphocreatinine

What is the Cori cycle?*
a. The coordinated muscle contraction sequence of slow- and fast-twitch muscles.
b. A process in the liver that regenerates glucose from lactic acid released by the muscles.
c. A standardized exercise protocol that measures VO2 max.
d. A series of enzymatic reactions to accelerate muscle glycogen repletion of muscles.
cards.back: b. A process in the liver that regenerates glucose from lactic acid released by the muscles.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. A process in the liver that regenerates glucose from lactic acid released by the muscles.

cards.front:
Which of the following would be the best choice for physically active people who need to rehydrate?*
a. “sweat” replacers
b. salt tablets in tap water
c. diluted juice or cool water
d. water warmed to body temperature
cards.back: c. diluted juice or cool water
cards.rationale: Answer: c. diluted juice or cool water

cards.front:
Under conditions of starvation, mobilization of body fat as fuel, especially for the brain and other nervous tissue, results in:*
a. Accumulation of alkaline compounds in the blood.
b. Elevated levels of ketones in the blood
c. Inadequate energy production to meet body needs
d. Inability to utilize glucose
cards.back: b. Elevated levels of ketones in the blood
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Elevated levels of ketones in the blood

cards.front:
Mrs. Reyes is scheduled to have her body fat measured by bioelectrical impedance. As a dietitian, you should explain that the test involves:*
a. Measurement of a fold of skin on the arm or abdomen, using calipers
b. Measurement of height and weight and plotting these in an equation
c. Weighing the patient while she is in an enclosed compartment
d. Attachment of electrodes to the extremities to measure resistance in the tissues
cards.back: d. Attachment of electrodes to the extremities to measure resistance in the tissues
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Attachment of electrodes to the extremities to measure resistance in the tissues

cards.front:
Which of the following clients would be at greatest risk for high blood pressure and breast cancer?*
a. Patient Z: waist = 27”, hip = 39”
b. Patient Y: waist = 30”, hip = 39”
c. Patient X: waist = 34”, hip = 40”
d. Patient W: waist = 24”, hip = 33”
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Patient X: waist = 34”, hip = 40”

cards.front:
The morbidly obese client who is surgically treated with gastroplasty is most likely to experience which complication after the surgery:*
a. High blood pressure
b. Dumping syndrome
c. Gallstones
d. Renal failure

Which of the following statements would be appropriate to make to a client for whom calcium supplements are prescribed:*
a. Take the supplements with apple juice
b. Take the supplement with vitamin D fortified milk
c. Dissolve the supplement in a solution of 1-part vinegar to 3 parts water before taking it
d. Increase intake of vitamin A to enhance calcium absorption
cards.back: b. Take the supplement with vitamin D fortified milk
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Take the supplement with vitamin D fortified milk

cards.front:
Vitamin C requirement is significantly increased in clients who*
a. have kidney stones
b. require anticonvulsant drugs
c. Have pernicious anemia
d. Smoke tobacco products

Vitamin D deficiency may be present in clients who*
a. have chronic renal failure
b. eat no animal products
c. fail to use sunscreens
d. use injectable narcotics
cards.rationale: Answer: a. have chronic renal failure

cards.front:
During the annual checkup of Gina, her mother informed you that their family has opted to exclude meat,poultry, and fish from their diet. You then advice Gina’s mother to:*
a. Give Gina vitamin B12 supplements
b. Include at least poultry or fish in Jina’s diet so she receives adequate amounts of essential fatty acids
c. Make sure Gina eats dark-green vegetables, fortified breads/cereals, and citrus juices
d. Have Gina take liquid protein supplements once a day
cards.back: a. Give Gina vitamin B12 supplements
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Give Gina vitamin B12 supplements

cards.front:
An individual with IDA should be encouraged to increase his/her intake of which of the following:*
a. dairy products
b. pasta
c. cruciferous vegetables
d. red meats

. What is the usual vitamin A deficiency sign?*
a. bone pain
b. bleeding gums
c. night blindness
d. seizures

The need for vitamin E in the diet will increase with an increase in the amount of what other nutrient in the diet?*
a. protein
b. saturated fatty acids
c. lipids
d. PUFA

Vitamin K deficiency is a possible result of*
a. kidney disease
b. antibiotic therapy
c. presence of phytates
d. low citrus fruits intake

Plant oils are excellent sources of _______ and liver is an excellent source of _______.*
a. vitamin K; vitamin A
b. vitamin E; vitamin D
c. vitamin E; vitamin A
d. vitamin D; vitamin K
cards.rationale: Answer: c. vitamin E; vitamin A

cards.front:
Which of the following people are least likely to need a vitamin/mineral supplement?*
a. pregnant or breast feeding mothers
b. vegans
c. male athletes
d. dieters on restricted energy intakes

There are studies that show that sodium and potassium have roles in the regulation of*
a. blood pressure
b. blood sugar level
c. lipid profile
d. blood composition

The mineral component of methionine, insulin, keratin, and glutathione is*
a. Manganese
b. Iodine
c. Iron
d. Sulfur

The mineral component of vitamin B12 is*
a. Iron
b. Zinc
c. Copper
d. Cobalt

Best type of exercise for physical conditioning is*
a. aerobic
b. anaerobic
c. calisthenics
d. jogging

Under normal conditions, the pH of the blood is*
a. slightly acidic
b. slightly basic
c. acidic
d. basic

Muscular fatigue during strenuous physical exercise is due to the accumulation of*
a. pyruvic acid
b. ammonia
c. lactic acid
d. HCl

Isoniazid, an anti-tuberculosis drug, is an antagonist of*
a. niacin
b. pyridoxine
c. folic acid
d. biotin

As a constituent of thiamine pyrophosphate and thiamine monophosphate, vitamin B1 is involved in themetabolism of*
a. glucose
b. amino acids
c. fatty acids
d. pentoses

The most variable component of total energy requirement is*
a. basal metabolic needs
b. energy cost of physical activities
c. thermic effect of food
d. respiratory quotient
cards.back: b. energy cost of physical activities
cards.rationale: Answer: b. energy cost of physical activities

cards.front:
The total energy of a food per 100 grams whose composition is 2% carbohydrates,18% protein, & 5% fat is*
a. 100 kcal
b. 125 kcal
c. 150 kcal
d. 200 kcal

The immediate source of energy for physical exercise is the*
a. phosphagen system consisting of stored ATP and creatine phosphate
b. anaerobic system
c. uerobic system
d. glycogen
cards.back: a. phosphagen system consisting of stored ATP and creatine phosphate
cards.rationale: Answer: a. phosphagen system consisting of stored ATP and creatine phosphate

cards.front:
The immediate need after strenuous exercise or physical activity*
a. fluid
b. simple carbohydrates
c. whey protein
d. salt

The only pentose of physiologic significance is*
a. mannose
b. ribose
c. arabinose
d. xylose

Vitamin D and parathyroid hormone promote*
a. calcium deposition in bones
b. calcium mobilization from the bones
c. urinary calcium excretion
d. fecal calcium excretion
cards.back: b. calcium mobilization from the bones
cards.rationale: Answer: b. calcium mobilization from the bones

cards.front:
The primary function of magnesium in metabolism is as a*
a. constituent of thyroxine
b. constituent of tissues
c. fluid balance regulator
d. coenzyme or enzyme activator
cards.rationale: Answer: d. coenzyme or enzyme activator

cards.front:
Mechanism by which body conserves iron stores*
a. by reusing iron released in the breakdown of red blood cells
b. by reducing iron content of hemoglobin
c. by regulating release of iron in the storage tissues
d. by increasing mucosal absorption of iron
cards.back: a. by reusing iron released in the breakdown of red blood cells
cards.rationale: Answer: a. by reusing iron released in the breakdown of red blood cells

decks.title: FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON FOOD SERVICE SYSTEMS
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON FOOD SERVICE SYSTEMS).

cards.front:
Which of the following is not a characteristic of a good cost control system?
A. Provides accurate, detailed, continuous data.
B. Designed to fit all types of food service operations
C. Simple to operate
D. Shows clear separation of duties
cards.back: B. Designed to fit all types of food service operations
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Designed to fit all types of food service operations

cards.front:
Which statement is not true about food cost?
A. It is the largest single cost element in foodservice
B. It is a variable cost
C. It is subject to price fluctuation
D. It is not manageable
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It is not manageable

cards.front:
Which of the following activities is not directly related to food cost control?
A. Generating management reports
B. Preventing wastes and inefficiencies
C. Improving service and satisfying customers
D. Reducing food related wastes & inefficiencies
cards.back: C. Improving service and satisfying customers
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Improving service and satisfying customers

cards.front:
Which of the following information is not provided in a standard recipe?
A. List of ingredients
B. Food cost
C. Recipe Yield
D. Portion size

Which statement is not true about popularity index?
A. It tells us how popular or acceptable a particular entrée is, at a particular period.
B. It guides us in projecting future sales for a particular entrée.
C. It signifies a trend in menu selection if the results are recurring.
D. It indicates the need to increase portion size of items served.
cards.back: D. It indicates the need to increase portion size of items served.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It indicates the need to increase portion size of items served.

cards.front:
A Chicken Macaroni soup recipe yields 6 quarts and portion size is ¾ cup How many portions will this recipe make?
A. 32 portions
B. 26 portions
C. 40 portions
D. 20 portions

As Purchased weight of Ox Tongue is 4 kilos and 700 grams. Edible weight after trimming and tenderizing is 3 kilos and 150 grams. Yield percentage is?
A. 60%
B. 70%
C. 82%
D. 67%

A standard recipe of Pancit Bihon yields 30 portions. I want to prepare 50 portions of this same recipe. How will I compute my scaling factor to determine how much of each ingredient I will need in my recipe?
A. Divide desired yield by the original yield
B. Multiply desired yield by original yield.
C. Divide original yield by desired yield
D. Multiply original yield by desired yield
cards.back: A. Divide desired yield by the original yield
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Divide desired yield by the original yield

cards.front:
The following practices contribute to high food cost except
A. cooking much more than what can be consumed and sold
B. doing recipe costing regularly to monitor changing costs
C. using requisition slip when withdrawing items from the storeroom
D. poor food storage thereby allowing food to spoil
cards.back: C. using requisition slip when withdrawing items from the storeroom
cards.rationale: Answer: C. using requisition slip when withdrawing items from the storeroom

cards.front:
The terms “crispy, moist, uniformly cooked and flavorful fried chicken “ are used to describe:
A. service standard
B. quality standard
C. cost standard
D. quantity standard

What does the term “consignment “ mean?
A. I leave my products with a seller for him to sell my products for a profit.
B. I sell my products on installment basis.
C. Someone sells my products for me without making profits
D. Someone buys my products and pays me in cash, then sell my products for profit.
cards.back: A. I leave my products with a seller for him to sell my products for a profit.
cards.rationale: Answer: A. I leave my products with a seller for him to sell my products for a profit.

cards.front:
Which of the following pricing methods is cost based?
A. Food cost pricing
B. Competitive pricing
C. Psychological pricing
D. Volume pricing

The following information can be found in a BUDGET except:
A. expected income and expenses.
B. activities to be undertaken for the period.
C. expected profit to be earned.
D. names of people hired and their respective positions.
cards.back: D. names of people hired and their respective positions.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. names of people hired and their respective positions.

cards.front:
A physical inventory is done at the end of each month for many reasons. Which is NOT a primary reason for doing a physical inventory?
A. To determine the value of the goods on hand, which is needed in making the financial statement
B. To check which items are slow moving and plan menus to make use of them before they spoil
C. To know what items need to be ordered from supplier
D. To clean the storeroom
cards.rationale: Answer: D. To clean the storeroom

cards.front:
Which of the following information is not found in a guest check ?
A. Cost of each item ordered
B. Date of transaction
C. Table number and name of server
D. Amount to be paid by each dine
cards.back: D. Amount to be paid by each dine
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Amount to be paid by each dine

cards.front:
An arrangement between buyer and supplier, whereby items are purchased in the exact time when the items are to be used is called
A. just in time purchasing
B. blanket purchase
C. prime vending
D. futures and contract method
cards.rationale: Answer: A. just in time purchasing

cards.front:
This method of pricing checks on prices for same product charged by nearby stores before finalizing their selling price.
A. Food cost %
B. Competitive pricing
C. What the market will bear
D. Volume pricing

This pricing method uses information on cost of ingredients and direct labor cost.
A. Prime cost %
B. Food cost %
C. Minimum sale pricing
D. Menu pricing multiplier

Compute for food cost percentage if sales for today is P58, 750 and actual food cost is P24, 675 .
A. 40%
B. 42%
C. 38 %
D. 50%

This type of inventory shows a running balance of each item stored, and is a continuous activity where the storekeeper always records items delivered and items withdrawn.
A. Turnover
B. Perpetual
C. Physical
D. On the spot

The following factors affect a restaurant’s labor cost except:
A. Labor laws and union agreements
B. Extensive use of convenience foods
C. Type of service
D. Daily menu combination

A restaurant had 3 cases of quart size canned pineapple juice ( 12 cans/case) at start of the month and used up 1 1/12 cases. How many cans must be purchased this month to bring the inventory back to the same starting level?
A. 12
B. 18
C. 24
D. 36

To control and manage my labor cost effectively, which of the following should I observe?
A. Setting productivity standards
B. Taking physical inventories
C. Setting standard portion sizes
D. Using standard recipes

When I use scoops to standardize my portions, what am I controlling
A. quality
B. quantity
C. inventory records
D. issuing

A restaurant served 120 guests for lunch today. Total sales for lunch was P45,000. What is the average check for lunch per guest?
A. P350
B. P375
C. P395
D. P345

If cost of inventory is P 32,380, and average inventory is P16,190, inventory turnover is _____
A.0.5
B. 1.0
C. 1.5
D. 2.0

A caterer earned P 55,000 sales for a dinner catering event and incurred a food cost of P28,000. What was the food cost percentage?
A. 48.7%
B. 43.5%
C. 50.9%
D. 43.5%

28. Labor cost is generally considered a fixed cost because monthly salary is a fixed amount and is not dependent on sales. Who among the following employees is likely to be receiving a salary considered as fixed- cost?
A. Dishwasher
B. Food Server
C. Supervisor
D. Utility worker

The normal quantity of a stored item required in a given operating period plus a safety factor for possible delay in delivery and for unexpected requirements, is called_______.
A. reorder point
B. balance on hand
C. par stock
D. perpetual inventory

Centralized purchasing is most appropriate for which type of operation
A. Food stall
B. School cafeteria
C. Chain restaurant
D. Coffee shop

The most important responsibility of a Receiving Clerk is to document deliveries and
A. order items
B. pay suppliers
C. negotiate discounts
D. check quality & quantity of deliveries
cards.back: D. check quality & quantity of deliveries
cards.rationale: Answer: D. check quality & quantity of deliveries

cards.front:
Upon receipt of delivered goods from the supplier, the Receiving Clerk (RC) should sign the _____.
A. invoice
B. specifications
C. purchase order
D. check for payment

Which of the following is most likely to be “direct” ?
A. Oysters
B. Canned Vienna Sausage
C. Raw potatoes
D. Bottled soda

Which of the following is not a method of menu analysis?
A. Meal Count
B. Menu engineering
C. Popularity index
D. recycling of left overs
cards.rationale: Answer: D. recycling of left overs

cards.front:
Which of the following best describes a standard recipe?
A. Instructions for preparing a dish
B. Tried and tested formula with consistent results
C. Recipe with the same taste always
D. The same recipe any time, any where
cards.back: B. Tried and tested formula with consistent results
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Tried and tested formula with consistent results

cards.front:
First-in-first- out (FIFO) is a method of
A. receiving deliveries
B. ordering food
C. rotating stock
D. maintaining storeroom security

Which of the following documents is used when issuing inventory supplies?
A. Purchase order
B. Purchase specifications
C. Requisition
D. invoice

If the portion size for Saba in Syrup is one piece whole banana, the portion is measured by
A. size
B. weight
C. count
D. container

How much is the portion cost of 100 grams of ground beef for hamburger if the cost of 1 kilo of ground beef is P600?
A. P 65
B. P 50
C. P 60
D. P 100

The edible meat from 1 kilo of scallops in a shell weighed 350 grams. What is the percentage of edible portion of this size and variety of scallops?
A. 35%
B. 30%
C. 350 %
D. 3.5%

A sales history is based on information taken from
A. perpetual inventories
B. requisitions
C. guest checks
D. production sheets

If 40 portions of Lamb Steak were sold out of 118 different entrees, what is its popularity index?
A. 20%
B. 34%
C. 41%
D. 52%

Menu items to be prepared each day are written on a
A. production list
B. bin card
C. sales history
D. requisition

A void sheet is used to record
A. sales errors made by the cashier
B. portions returned by customers
C. food items needed from inventory
D. food items that are wasted
cards.rationale: Answer: B. portions returned by customers

cards.front:
When we do an actual count of all items kept in the storeroom, we are doing a ____.
A. physical inventory
B. inventory evaluation
C. inventory turnover
D. perpetual inventory

To compute for cost of food sold, add purchases to opening inventory, and subtract ____.
A. gross margin
B. closing inventory
C. cost of deliveries
D. requisitions

Foods categorized as “directs” are
A. charged to cost immediately upon delivery
B. verified against a purchase order
C. charged to cost when issued from inventory
D. verified against an invoice
cards.back: A. charged to cost immediately upon delivery
cards.rationale: Answer: A. charged to cost immediately upon delivery

cards.front:
Labor cost is generally considered a ______ cost because it is not dependent on sales.
A. Fixed
B. Variable
C. Prime
D. Non controllable

Food cost of Mixed Grilled Platter is P245.00. When sold at P P612.50, what is the food cost percentage?
A. 35 %
B 36.5%
C. 38 %
D. 40 %

My standard recipe for Chicken Pastel is good for 50 portions at 1 cup per portion. Compute for scaling factor if I will prepare the same standard recipe for 35 portions.
A. 1.7
B. 0.7
C. 1.5
D. 12

51. The principle which states that “each employee must know to whom he reports”, refers to
A. departmentation
B. delegation of authority
C. unity of command
D. delegation of responsibility

In applying the principle of span of control, one needs to consider the following except
A. number of people to be supervised
B. supervision & attention needed to do job
C. the salary of the people involved
D. managerial capability of the supervisor
cards.back: C. the salary of the people involved
cards.rationale: Answer: C. the salary of the people involved

cards.front:
Which action is contrary to the principle of homogenous assignment ?
A. Group workers who perform similar functions .
B. Limit the variety of jobs assigned to an employee
C. Assign an employee to perform several secondary unrelated jobs.
D. Reduce employees’ job inefficiency and confusion
cards.back: C. Assign an employee to perform several secondary unrelated jobs.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Assign an employee to perform several secondary unrelated jobs.

cards.front:
Which of the following information is not reflected in the organizational chart?
A. Duplication of functions
B. An overloaded manager
C. Important functions neglected or overstressed
D. Specific responsibilities of managers
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Specific responsibilities of managers

cards.front:
A manager who waits for situations to arise before taking action is described as ______ manager.
A. doer
B. proactive
C. facilitator
D. reactive

Which statement does not conform with the traditional principles of management?
A. The interest of the organization is more important than those of any individual/group in the organization.
B. Decision making authority should rest at the top level of the organization
C. The same plan should be followed for a group of activities that have the same goal or objective.
D. Employees can receive orders from different bosses.
cards.back: D. Employees can receive orders from different bosses.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Employees can receive orders from different bosses.

cards.front:
A leader who uses appropriate supportive & directive behaviors based on the situation is called a ___ leader.
A. transactional
B. situational
C. flexible
D. transformational

The type of leadership where employees are not given a voice on company matters, and practically everything is dictated by the company is called.
A. Transactional
B. Democratic
C. Transformational
D. Autocratic

Which theory says workers are lazy and must be directed and forced to do their work?
A. Maslow’s Theory
B. Hawthorne’s Theory
C. Theory X
D. Theory Y

Which theory describes workers as committed to their job and want to achieve meaningful results?
A. Maslow’s Theory
B. Herzberg’s Theory
C. Theory X
D. Theory Y

Which management function involves inspiring and motivating staff to willingly get the work done?*
A. Planning
B.Organizing
C. Leading
D. Controlling

Supervisors must direct the work of their people so that they will do their work
A. voluntarily
B. and stay on the job
C. at their own pace
D. as directed

Authority derived by virtue of one’s position is called _____ authority.
A. informal
B. staff
C. formal
D. line

Leaders who lead by virtue of the support given by fellow employees are called ______ leaders.
A. Transactional
B. transformational
C. formal leaders
D. informal

A detailed outline of routine tasks and side duties for each job position is called
A. Job standards
B. Job description
C. Job Specification
D. Job Classification

An employee’s dissatisfaction for unjust company disciplinary action against him is called a…..
A. disciplinary action
B. corrective action
C. discipline
D. grievance

A corrective action by the company to make employees understand and follow company rules.
A. Discipline
B. Corrective interview
C. Consultation
D. Grievance

An outline of the personal qualification requirements for each position is called
A. Job standards
B. Job description
C. Job specification
D. Job classification

The Labor Code of the Philippines is embodied in
A. PD 440
B. PD 442
C. PD 540
D. PD 542

A disagreement among individuals/groups in an organization results in
A. Harassment
B. Conflict
C. Discipline
D. Grievance

As per Labor Code, which situation does not warrant requiring employees to work overtime?
A. National/local emergency
B. Urgent office work to be performed
C. Urgent need to prevent loss of lives or damage to goods
D. An absent manager or supervisor
cards.back: D. An absent manager or supervisor
cards.rationale: Answer: D. An absent manager or supervisor

cards.front:
Which is not required for a woman to avail of maternity leave?
A. 6 months service for the last 12 months
B. woman must be in her first four deliveries
C. legally married
D. submission of medical certificate

A supervisor who evaluates and compares results with targets and standards previously set, is performing what management function?
A. planning
B. organizing
C. leading
D. controlling

As per Labor Code, the normal daily hours of work for any employee is
A. 9 hours
B. 8 hours
C. 10 hours
D. 12 hours

“Hours worked” as defined by the Labor Code, refers to
A. duty hours + short rest periods
B. duty hours - short rest periods
C duty hours + short rest periods + 1hr lunch break
D. duty hours + short rest periods - 1hr lunch break
cards.back: A. duty hours + short rest periods
cards.rationale: Answer: A. duty hours + short rest periods

cards.front:
As per Labor Code, our overtime (OT) practice is wrong if we ____________
A. give at least 25% of regular wage as OT pay
B. offset OT by going under time on another day
C. ask employees to work OT in an emergency
D. give 40% of pay for OT work rendered
cards.back: B. offset OT by going under time on another day
cards.rationale: Answer: B. offset OT by going under time on another day

cards.front:
As per Labor Code, which statement related to holidays is incorrect?
A. Companies w/ 5 or less employees are exempted from giving regular pay during regular holidays
B. Compensation for employees working on holidays should be twice his regular rate
C. Employer determines employees’ schedule & weekly rest day
D. Religion should be considered in determining rest day
cards.back: A. Companies w/ 5 or less employees are exempted from giving regular pay during regular holidays
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Companies w/ 5 or less employees are exempted from giving regular pay during regular holidays

cards.front:
The following are functions of human resource management except ________
A. Recruiting potential employees
B. Screening applicants
C. Attracting potential job seekers to apply
D. Developing standards for food and beverage
cards.back: D. Developing standards for food and beverage
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Developing standards for food and beverage

cards.front:
Human resource management does not involve ______
A. orienting employees
B. resolving conflicts
C. controlling food cost for employees’ meals
D. supervising employees
cards.back: C. controlling food cost for employees’ meals
cards.rationale: Answer: C. controlling food cost for employees’ meals

cards.front:
Which of the following is not true about job analysis?
A. It is a detailed, systematic study of jobs
B. It aims to determine the duties and responsibilities of a particular position
C. It includes the study of working conditions and working relationships
D. It is a study of the salary scale structure for employees
cards.back: D. It is a study of the salary scale structure for employees
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It is a study of the salary scale structure for employees

cards.front:
A job analysis is used for the following purposes, except
A. to guide in employee recruitment, selection and placement.
B. to outline employee job opportunities within the company.
C. to provide information on possible training needs/programs to be conducted.
D. to determine job satisfaction level of employees
cards.back: D. to determine job satisfaction level of employees
cards.rationale: Answer: D. to determine job satisfaction level of employees

cards.front:
What is the sequence of steps involved in selection and hiring of employees?
A. Recruitment, testing, application, matching, interviews, orientation, hiring
B. Recruitment, interviews, application, selection, hiring, orientation
C. Recruitment, application, testing, interviews, matching, hiring, orientation
D. Recruitment, orientation, interviews, application, hiring
cards.back: C. Recruitment, application, testing, interviews, matching, hiring, orientation
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Recruitment, application, testing, interviews, matching, hiring, orientation

cards.front:
Which of the following information is not true about a job description?
A. It contains information on what the job is and the specific duties involved
B. It shows the responsibilities and general conditions related to the job
C. It defines the scope of a job, and sets boundaries between positions
D. It gives information on rules and regulations related to the job
cards.back: D. It gives information on rules and regulations related to the job
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It gives information on rules and regulations related to the job

cards.front:
Job shadowing is a commonly used training method in foodservice operations. What is job shadowing?
A. When a more experienced mentor is assigned to coach the trainee
B. When employees are orated from one job to another, to learn and familiarize themselves with different jobs
C. When a trainee attends several training sessions conducted by experienced employees acting as mentors
D. When a trainee learns from a more experience employee by following anf observing him as he does his daily work
cards.back: D. When a trainee learns from a more experience employee by following anf observing him as he does his daily work
cards.rationale: Answer: D. When a trainee learns from a more experience employee by following anf observing him as he does his daily work

cards.front:
Which of the following is not an expected immediate benefit derived by an employee who undergoes training?
A. Improves employees’ skills, knowledge & attitude
B. It raises employee’s pay
C. It improves quality of work.
D. Contributes to mployee’s growth & development
cards.rationale: Answer: B. It raises employee’s pay

cards.front:
The Buddy Method is _______
A. a formal type of employee training used in restaurants
B. an informal method of training done before an employee is hired
C. an informal type of training where an employee is paired with another
D. a seminar type of training where employees are gathered in a session hall
cards.back: C. an informal type of training where an employee is paired with another
cards.rationale: Answer: C. an informal type of training where an employee is paired with another

cards.front:
Which of the general statements below about adult training is not correct.
A. Adults learn by doing & being actively involved.
B. Instruction must be designed based on trainees’ needs .
C. Training content and subject matter must be relevant.
D. Adults are more knowledgeable than young trainees
cards.back: D. Adults are more knowledgeable than young trainees
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Adults are more knowledgeable than young trainees

cards.front:
Which statement is not true about adult learning?
A. Adults learn more when activities are participative and hands on.
B. Adults learners are usually more confident than young learners.
C. Training is more effective when adult learns are given feedback on how well they are performing.
D. Adults often doubt their ability to learn, and fear embarrassment and failure.
cards.back: B. Adults learners are usually more confident than young learners.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Adults learners are usually more confident than young learners.

cards.front:
The following are objectives of performance appraisal except __________
A. to verify if supervisors know how tor ate their employees effectively
B. to have basis for pay increases, employee recognition and awards
C. to document unsatisfactory performance
D. to serve as basis for giving bonuses and incentives
cards.back: A. to verify if supervisors know how tor ate their employees effectively
cards.rationale: Answer: A. to verify if supervisors know how tor ate their employees effectively

cards.front:
The following are usually evaluated in an employee performance appraisal, except
A. quality and quantity of work done
B. attendance
C. attitude and cooperation
D. competence of the rating supervisor
cards.back: D. competence of the rating supervisor
cards.rationale: Answer: D. competence of the rating supervisor

cards.front:
What should guide supervisors when rating the performance of their staff?
A. Exercise objectivity at all times
B. Halo effect
C. Horn effect
D. Procrastination
cards.back: A. Exercise objectivity at all times
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Exercise objectivity at all times

cards.front:
An Italian royalty credited for the development of French cuisine. She married the King of France, and moved to live there, bringing with her, her Italian chefs and knowledge of food preparation and service, which spawned the development of French Cuisine.
A. Marie Antoinette
B. Florence Nightingale
C. Catherine de Medici
D. Andrea Bocelli

The person who is over all in charge of the kitchen , and directs everything in the kitchen, based on an organized kitchen brigade.
A. Chef de Cuisine or Executive Chef
B. Sous chef
C. Commis
D. Chef de Partie
cards.back: A. Chef de Cuisine or Executive Chef
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Chef de Cuisine or Executive Chef

cards.front:
In the classical kitchen brigade system, the person responsible for preparing fish dishes is called
A. Saucier
B. Rottiseur
C. Potager
D. Poissonier

A chef de partie who is responsible for the cold kitchen is called
A. garde manger
B. saucier
C. grillardin
D. poissonier
