What do restaurant services, like delivery service, take out, and fast food service offer in common?
A. Fancy food
B. Gourmet food
C. Quickie food
D. Convenience

Regarded as a win-win business arrangement where a mother company gives the right to another company to use its business concept, sells its products, in exchange for a fee.
A. Leasing
B. Franchising
C. Partnership
D. Subsidiary

This term refers to nationality restaurants, like Japanese, Vietnamese, etc. that feature country cuisine.
A. Specialty
B. Ethnic
C. Casual dining
D. Theme

He is a known as the Father of Canning, who made possible the preservation of food and prevention of food spoilage using hermetically sealed containers, and in 1809 made possible preservation of food for the use of the army and navy in France.
A. Delmonico
B. Louis Pasteur
C. Nicolas Appert
D. Marie Antoine Caremer

This chef is known for having organized the kitchen brigade system and the classical organization of the kitchen.
A. Marie Antoine Careme
B. Auguste Escoffier
C. Anthelme Brillat Savartin
D. Francois Pierre La Varene

decks.title: FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON FUNDAMENTALS IN FOOD AND COOKERY
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (FFSS :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON FUNDAMENTALS IN FOOD AND COOKERY).

cards.front:
Why is steaming preferred over boiling for cooking green vegetables when the goal is to maximize nutrient retention?
A. Steaming maintains a higher cooking temperature.
B. Boiling enhances the flavor through leaching.
C. Steaming prevents loss of water-soluble vitamins into the cooking liquid.
D. Boiling preserves more enzymes needed for digestion
cards.back: C. Steaming prevents loss of water-soluble vitamins into the cooking liquid.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Steaming prevents loss of water-soluble vitamins into the cooking liquid.

cards.front:
A food technologist is designing a process to minimize enzymatic browning in freshly sliced apples while enhancing flavor and color during baking. Which of the following best explains why applying heat serves this dual purpose?
A. Heat promotes Maillard browning and accelerates the activity of polyphenol oxidase, increasing overall browning.
B. Heat inactivates enzymes responsible for enzymatic browning and initiates Maillard browning, contributing to color and flavor.
C. Enzymatic browning occurs at high temperatures, while Maillard browning is prevented by heat due to sugar caramelization.
D. Heating encourages enzymatic browning through protein denaturation and prevents the Maillard reaction by breaking down amino acids.
cards.back: B. Heat inactivates enzymes responsible for enzymatic browning and initiates Maillard browning, contributing to color and flavor.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Heat inactivates enzymes responsible for enzymatic browning and initiates Maillard browning, contributing to color and flavor.

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains why kneading is essential for proper gluten development in yeast-leavened dough?
A. Kneading warms the dough, accelerating yeast fermentation.
B. Kneading introduces more flour, which strengthens the dough.
C. Kneading aligns gluten strands, forming an elastic network that traps gas.
D. Kneading dissolves gluten proteins to form a smoother texture.
cards.back: C. Kneading aligns gluten strands, forming an elastic network that traps gas.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Kneading aligns gluten strands, forming an elastic network that traps gas.

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains why a starch-thickened sauce becomes watery when subjected to excessive heat for a prolonged period?
A. Gelatinization causes starch granules to swell and burst, increasing the viscosity of the mixture.
B. Dextrinization enhances the thickening power of starch by breaking it into smaller chains.
C. Excessive heat disrupts starch micelles, leading to a breakdown of the gel structure and resulting in a watery consistency.
D. Higher temperatures always increase the thickening ability of starch due to continuous gelatinization.
cards.back: C. Excessive heat disrupts starch micelles, leading to a breakdown of the gel structure and resulting in a watery consistency.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Excessive heat disrupts starch micelles, leading to a breakdown of the gel structure and resulting in a watery consistency.

cards.front:
Why should acidic ingredients like tomato juice or molasses be added only after beans have become tender during cooking?
A. Acids increase the rate of gelatinization, softening beans too quickly
B. Acids neutralize the beans’ natural flavor and aroma
C. Acids toughen cellulose, delaying softening and prolonging cooking time
D. Acids remove pigments that affect color and texture of beans
cards.back: C. Acids toughen cellulose, delaying softening and prolonging cooking time
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Acids toughen cellulose, delaying softening and prolonging cooking time

cards.front:
Why is open kettle cooking recommended when preparing strong-flavored vegetables such as cabbage or radish?
A. It prevents oxidation of nutrients by limiting air exposure
B. It allows sulfur compounds to escape, reducing strong odors and flavors
C. It retains more chlorophyll for greener appearance
D. It speeds up cooking by increasing pressure inside the pot
cards.back: B. It allows sulfur compounds to escape, reducing strong odors and flavors
cards.rationale: Answer: B. It allows sulfur compounds to escape, reducing strong odors and flavors

cards.front:
Why does cooking beans in hard water take longer compared to soft water?
A. The minerals in hard water enhance bean flavor but reduce the temperature.
B. Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water form insoluble salts with pectin, slowing the softening.
C. Hard water contains fewer electrolytes needed for heat transfer.
D. Beans absorb less water in hard water due to its higher boiling point
cards.back: B. Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water form insoluble salts with pectin, slowing the softening.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water form insoluble salts with pectin, slowing the softening.

cards.front:
Why is it advisable to add acidic ingredients (like vinegar or calamansi) at the end of cooking green vegetables such as kangkong in dishes like sinigang?
A. Acids enhance the texture of vegetables by making them firmer.
B. Acids speed up the cooking process by increasing the temperature.
C. Acids preserve chlorophyll, maintaining the bright green color of vegetables.
D. Acids promote the formation of pheophytin, causing a dull or olive green color if added early.
cards.back: D. Acids promote the formation of pheophytin, causing a dull or olive green color if added early.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Acids promote the formation of pheophytin, causing a dull or olive green color if added early.

cards.front:
Tough cuts of red meat are best prepared using moist-heat methods because they:
A. Are low in protein and fat.
B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.
C. Easily disintegrate in dry heat.
D. Contain more water-soluble vitamins.
cards.back: B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.

cards.front:
Searing red meat before braising enhances flavor by:
A. Boiling away surface bacteria.
B. Sealing in internal moisture.
C. Promoting Maillard browning reactions on the surface.
D. Breaking down muscle fibers instantly.
cards.back: C. Promoting Maillard browning reactions on the surface.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Promoting Maillard browning reactions on the surface.

cards.front:
Tough cuts of red meat are best prepared using moist-heat methods because they:
A. Are low in protein and fat.
B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.
C. Easily disintegrate in dry heat.
D. Contain more water-soluble vitamins
cards.back: B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Have high amounts of connective tissue that require longer cooking to soften.

cards.front:
Grilling is most suitable for tender cuts of red meat because it:
A. Requires minimal fat content.
B. Cooks meat through internal steam.
C. Prevents any protein denaturation.
D. Uses high, direct heat to quickly sear the exterior.
cards.back: D. Uses high, direct heat to quickly sear the exterior.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Uses high, direct heat to quickly sear the exterior.

cards.front:
Braising improves the tenderness of red meat by:
A. Slowly cooking the meat in a small amount of liquid.
B. Steaming the meat at high pressure.
C. Applying intense dry heat directly.
D. Charring the outer surface at high temperature.
cards.back: A. Slowly cooking the meat in a small amount of liquid.
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Slowly cooking the meat in a small amount of liquid.

cards.front:
Which cooking method uses radiant heat from above and is ideal for melting fat and creating a crust on meats like pork chops or steaks?
A. Boiling
B. Broiling
C. Steaming
D. Roasting

What combination cooking method begins by searing meat, then simmering it in a small amount of liquid, ideal for tough pork or beef cuts?
A. Broiling
B. Braising
C. Poaching
D. Deep frying

When a tough cut of meat like beef brisket is cooked in liquid over low heat for a long period, the method used is:
A. Roasting
B. Steaming
C. Stewing
D. Sautéing

Which cooking method is most suitable for tender cuts of meat, such as pork loin or beef sirloin, to preserve juiciness and flavor?
A. Boiling
B. Grilling
C. Braising
D. Stewing

The meat cut likely to be most tender comes from the least exercised part of the animal.
A. Neck
B. Chuck
C. Tenderloin
D. Shank

A variety of meat considered rich in iron and used in both Western and Asian cuisines is:
A. Tripe
B. Sirloin
C. Drumstick
D. Rump

Which of the following requires moist-heat cooking?
A. Breast, because it has the most muscle activity
B. Thigh, because it is a lean and rarely used part
C. Back and legs, because they are less tender due to frequent use
D. Wings, because they are fatty and tender
cards.back: C. Back and legs, because they are less tender due to frequent use
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Back and legs, because they are less tender due to frequent use

cards.front:
Crustaceans such as crabs and lobsters change color from dark green or blue to bright orange-red when cooked because:
A. Their shells are exposed to steam, which softens pigments.
B. The muscle tissues absorb heat and change hue.
C. Heat causes protein-bound pigments like astaxanthin to be released.
D. Oxygen from boiling water reacts with shell minerals.
cards.back: C. Heat causes protein-bound pigments like astaxanthin to be released.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Heat causes protein-bound pigments like astaxanthin to be released.

cards.front:
Trimethylamine oxide (TMAO), naturally present in fish muscle, is converted into trimethylamine (TMA), producing a stale fish odor, due to the action of the enzyme:
A. Lipase
B. Protease
C. Trimethylamine oxidase (TMAOase)
D. Catalase

Fish cooks faster than chicken, pork, or beef because it contains:
A. More connective tissue and dense muscle fibers
B. Tougher myofibrillar proteins
C. Less connective tissue and no elastin
D. Higher amounts of saturated fat
cards.back: C. Less connective tissue and no elastin
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Less connective tissue and no elastin

cards.front:
Which cooking method is most appropriate for lean fish with delicate muscle structure and minimal connective tissue?
A. Braising
B. Stewing
C. Grilling
D. Poaching

Why are duck eggs generally preferred over chicken eggs for salt curing, such as in the preparation of salted eggs?
A. Because duck eggs have a thicker shell that absorbs salt faster.
B. Because duck eggs have a higher fat content in the yolk, resulting in a richer texture and flavor after curing.
C. Because duck eggs are smaller and cure more evenly in brine solutions.
D. Because duck eggs contain less water, allowing the salt to concentrate better in the yolk.
cards.back: B. Because duck eggs have a higher fat content in the yolk, resulting in a richer texture and flavor after curing.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Because duck eggs have a higher fat content in the yolk, resulting in a richer texture and flavor after curing.

cards.front:
Why does overheating eggs beyond 70°C typically result in a tough and rubbery texture?
A. Because the yolk fats evaporate, leaving behind only dense proteins.
B. Because the egg proteins coagulate excessively, squeezing out water and forming a tight network.
C. Because the sugar in the egg caramelizes, hardening the mixture.
D. Because the egg white becomes diluted at high temperatures, making it less flexible.
cards.back: B. Because the egg proteins coagulate excessively, squeezing out water and forming a tight network.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Because the egg proteins coagulate excessively, squeezing out water and forming a tight network.

cards.front:
In baked goods such as cakes and custards, how do eggs function as structural and textural agents?
A. Eggs contribute moisture only and do not affect texture or structure.
B. Eggs prevent browning, keeping the product pale and soft.
C. Eggs break down starches, making the product denser and chewier.
D. Eggs coagulate during heating, helping form structure and a tender, fluffy texture.
cards.back: D. Eggs coagulate during heating, helping form structure and a tender, fluffy texture.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Eggs coagulate during heating, helping form structure and a tender, fluffy texture.

cards.front:
Why are eggs considered excellent emulsifying agents in food preparation such as in mayonnaise or cake batters?
A. Because egg whites contain proteins that prevent oil and water from separating.
B. Because egg yolks contain lecithin, which stabilizes emulsions by binding fat and water.
C. Because eggs are high in fat, which dissolves both oil and water easily.
D. Because the whole egg forms foams that naturally keep mixtures stable.
cards.back: D. Because the whole egg forms foams that naturally keep mixtures stable.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Because the whole egg forms foams that naturally keep mixtures stable.

cards.front:
Why do eggs whip better at room temperature compared to when they are taken directly from the refrigerator?
A. Because room temperature eggs contain more air, which helps in foam formation.
B. Because the proteins in room temperature eggs unfold more easily, allowing better foam structure.
C. Because refrigeration adds water to the eggs, diluting the proteins needed for foaming.
D. Because warm eggs are heavier and create more stable peaks when beaten.
cards.back: B. Because the proteins in room temperature eggs unfold more easily, allowing better foam structure.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Because the proteins in room temperature eggs unfold more easily, allowing better foam structure.

cards.front:
What is the effect of adding an acid, such as cream of tartar or lemon juice, early in the whipping of egg whites?
A. It delays foaming but produces a more stable foam by strengthening protein structure.
B. It immediately increases foam volume but causes the foam to collapse quickly.
C. It prevents the egg whites from incorporating air, making whipping ineffective.
D. It reacts with egg white sugars to form a stiff, dry foam.
cards.back: A. It delays foaming but produces a more stable foam by strengthening protein structure.
cards.rationale: Answer: A. It delays foaming but produces a more stable foam by strengthening protein structure.

cards.front:
Why do eggs demonstrate excellent binding capacity in recipes such as meatballs, croquettes, or batters?
A. Because egg yolks are high in fat, which glues ingredients together.
B. Because egg whites contain starch that thickens and binds ingredients.
C. Because eggs contain sugar that caramelizes and locks ingredients in place.
D. Because egg proteins coagulate when heated, holding ingredients in a firm structure.
cards.back: D. Because egg proteins coagulate when heated, holding ingredients in a firm structure.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Because egg proteins coagulate when heated, holding ingredients in a firm structure.

cards.front:
Why does evaporated milk whip better when chilled?
A. Water evaporates faster
B. Fat solidifies, increasing viscosity
C. Protein denaturation occurs
D. Sugar crystallizes
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Fat solidifies, increasing viscosity

cards.front:
What is the main difference between yogurt and buttermilk?
A. Yogurt is fermented; buttermilk is not
B. Buttermilk has more sugar
C. Yogurt uses whole or skim milk; buttermilk uses skim milk
D. Yogurt contains more water
cards.back: C. Yogurt uses whole or skim milk; buttermilk uses skim milk
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Yogurt uses whole or skim milk; buttermilk uses skim milk

cards.front:
What is the effect of adding sugar too early during cream whipping?
A. Increases whipping time
B. Helps stabilize foam
C. Reduces volume
D. Prevents curdling

Which of the following is the most critical factor in successfully whipping cream?
A. High sugar content
B. High lactose content
C. Cold temperature
D. Low fat content

Which fat content range is ideal for whipping cream?
A. 10–15%
B. 20–25%
C. 30–36%
D. 40–50%

Which of the following best describes "filled evaporated milk"?
A. Milk with added sugar
B. Milk with vegetable fat instead of milk fat
C. Milk with reduced lactose
D. Milk enriched with vitamins
cards.back: B. Milk with vegetable fat instead of milk fat
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Milk with vegetable fat instead of milk fat

cards.front:
Why is fructose considered the best sugar to prevent crystallization when cooking crystalline candies?
A. It is less sweet than glucose, so it allows higher concentrations in solution.
B. It caramelizes quickly, preventing crystal formation.
C. It has the highest molecular weight among sugars, increasing viscosity.
D. It is the hardest common sugar to crystallize, helping control texture.
cards.back: D. It is the hardest common sugar to crystallize, helping control texture.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It is the hardest common sugar to crystallize, helping control texture.

cards.front:
How does sugar contribute to the tender texture of baked products such as cakes and cookies?
A. By increasing the protein content of flour
B. By absorbing excess water from the batter
C. By competing with flour for water, slowing gluten development
D. By reacting with baking soda to produce more air
cards.back: C. By competing with flour for water, slowing gluten development
cards.rationale: Answer: C. By competing with flour for water, slowing gluten development

cards.front:
Which of the following statements best explains why coconut oil is solid at room temperature, unlike most other vegetable oils?
A. It is composed mainly of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids.
B. It is high in monoglycerides, which are more stable at room temperature.
C. It contains mostly medium-chain saturated fatty acids.
D. It is rich in triglycerides with unsaturated bonds that crystallize easily.
cards.back: C. It contains mostly medium-chain saturated fatty acids.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It contains mostly medium-chain saturated fatty acids.

cards.front:
Which market form of fat is best suited for creaming and baking applications because of its plasticity?
A. Salad oil
B. Table fat
C. Cooking oil
D. Shortening

Why is butter typically soft at room temperature compared to beef tallow?
A. It contains smaller fat crystals.
B. It has undergone winterization.
C. It is composed of mostly unsaturated fatty acids.
D. It has a high smoke point.
cards.back: C. It is composed of mostly unsaturated fatty acids.
cards.rationale:
Answer:
C. It is composed of mostly unsaturated fatty acids.

cards.front:
Why are lard, butter, margarine, and suet called shortening?
A. It melts quickly at high temperatures, shortening the cooking time.
B. It increases the shelf life of baked products.
C. It coats flour particles, limiting gluten formation and "shortening" gluten strands.
D. It causes baked goods to rise faster by shortening proofing time.
cards.back: C. It coats flour particles, limiting gluten formation and "shortening" gluten strands.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It coats flour particles, limiting gluten formation and "shortening" gluten strands.

cards.front:
The correct classification of a bird that has been slaughtered, bled, defeathered, with head and feet removed is:
A. Whole or Galantina
B. Dressed
C. Ready-to-cook
D. Live

A chef prepares two batches of beef stew—one simmered for 2 hours, and another simmered for only 20 minutes. Based on the effect of cooking duration on flavor, which statement best explains the difference in flavor between the two?
A. The short-cooked stew develops more umami due to faster protein coagulation.
B. The long-cooked stew has deeper flavor because prolonged heat breaks down fat and protein into flavorful compounds.
C. The short-cooked stew retains more natural meat flavor due to minimal protein denaturation.
D. The long-cooked stew loses flavor because the volatile aroma compounds evaporate completely.
cards.back: B. The long-cooked stew has deeper flavor because prolonged heat breaks down fat and protein into flavorful compounds.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. The long-cooked stew has deeper flavor because prolonged heat breaks down fat and protein into flavorful compounds.

cards.front:
Which of the following rice types is most suitable for sticky desserts such as suman or biko?
A. IR 8, because it has high amylose content and remains separate when cooked.
B. Milagrosa, because it has intermediate amylose content and a soft texture.
C. Waxy rice (malagkit), because it has virtually no amylose and becomes sticky when cooked.
D. Basmati, because it is aromatic and elongates on cooking.
cards.back: C. Waxy rice (malagkit), because it has virtually no amylose and becomes sticky when cooked.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Waxy rice (malagkit), because it has virtually no amylose and becomes sticky when cooked.

cards.front:
A student wanted to cook champorado with a thick consistency. She used a 2:1 water-to-rice ratio and added milk and sugar at the beginning of cooking. The final product turned out thick but slightly undercooked. What is the most likely reason for the undercooked texture?
A. She used too much water for champorado.
B. Sugar and milk were added too early, delaying gelatinization.
C. The rice was over-agitated during cooking.
D. She should have used cold water instead of hot water.
cards.back: B. Sugar and milk were added too early, delaying gelatinization.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Sugar and milk were added too early, delaying gelatinization.

cards.front:
Which of the following will result in a fluffy and separate-grained texture when cooking rice?
A. Using more water and starting with cold water
B. Soaking the rice and using hard water
C. Starting with hot water and using the correct rice-to-water ratio
D. Stirring rice frequently during cooking
cards.back: C. Starting with hot water and using the correct rice-to-water ratio
cards.rationale:
Answer:
C. Starting with hot water and using the correct rice-to-water ratio

cards.front:
Brown rice is considered more nutritious than white rice primarily because:
A. It is a processed cereal.
B. It contains added nutrients.
C. It is milled with only the hull removed, retaining the bran and germ.
D. It is highly milled and polished for easy digestion.
cards.back: C. It is milled with only the hull removed, retaining the bran and germ.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It is milled with only the hull removed, retaining the bran and germ.

cards.front:
Which of the following functional properties of starch is most responsible for the firming of custards and pie fillings after cooling?
A. Viscosity
B. Gelatinization
C. Retrogradation
D. Gel formation

Which of the following best explains why waxy starches are preferred in products requiring freeze-thaw stability (e.g., frozen pie fillings)?
A. They contain high amylose content
B. They are resistant to syneresis due to high amylopectin
C. They swell less during gelatinization
D. They retrograde faster
cards.back: C. They swell less during gelatinization
cards.rationale: Answer: C. They swell less during gelatinization

cards.front:
Why does continuous stirring during the cooking of starch mixtures lead to a pasty consistency?
A. It enhances retrogradation
B. It causes over-gelatinization
C. It breaks down starch granules, releasing more amylose
D. It prevents starch swelling
cards.back: C. It breaks down starch granules, releasing more amylose
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It breaks down starch granules, releasing more amylose

cards.front:
In which food product is starch primarily used for its moisture-retention properties?
A. Pudding
B. Bread
C. Jelly
D. Peanut butter

Which of the following situations will most likely result in a firmer gel during starch gelatinization?
A. Adding sugar and acid before heating
B. Cooking with direct heat and stirring continuously
C. Using milk and eggs with minimal stirring
D. Using low starch concentration and high agitation
cards.back: C. Using milk and eggs with minimal stirring
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Using milk and eggs with minimal stirring

cards.front:
A baker notices that her muffins have developed large tunnels and a tough texture. Which factor most likely caused this issue?
A. Using soft wheat flour instead of hard wheat flour
B. Undermixing the batter during preparation
C. Overmixing the batter using the muffin method
D. Using cake flour instead of all-purpose flour
cards.back: C. Overmixing the batter using the muffin method
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Overmixing the batter using the muffin method

cards.front:
A cook preparing popovers follows the correct flour-liquid ratio but ends up with flat and soggy results. Which of the following is the most likely factor affecting the product quality?
A. Use of soft wheat flour instead of hard flour
B. Use of the pastry method instead of the straight dough method
C. Incorrect oven temperature or improper placement in the oven
D. Use of stainless steel pans instead of glass pans
cards.back: C. Incorrect oven temperature or improper placement in the oven
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Incorrect oven temperature or improper placement in the oven

cards.front:
Which of the following combinations would most likely delay gluten development in a flour mixture?
A. Bread flour, water, and yeast
B. Cake flour, water, and salt
C. All-purpose flour, sugar, fat, and lemon juice
D. High-protein flour and vigorous kneading
cards.back: C. All-purpose flour, sugar, fat, and lemon juice
cards.rationale: Answer: C. All-purpose flour, sugar, fat, and lemon juice

cards.front:
In which scenario will yeast activity be compromised, affecting the leavening process of bread?
A. Using active dry yeast at 42°C
B. Using compressed yeast stored at 5°C
C. Using quick-rising yeast at room temperature
D. Using active dry yeast in water at 25°C
cards.back: A. Using active dry yeast at 42°C
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Using active dry yeast at 42°C

cards.front:
Which of the following combinations would most likely result in a dense and poorly risen cake, assuming all other factors are constant?
A. Bread flour, baking soda, no acidic ingredient
B. Cake flour, baking soda, lemon juice
C. All-purpose flour, baking powder, milk
D. All-purpose flour, baking powder, vinegar
cards.back: A. Bread flour, baking soda, no acidic ingredient
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Bread flour, baking soda, no acidic ingredient

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains why fat is referred to as a "shortening" in flour mixtures?
A. It shortens the baking time of products.
B. It prevents sugar from dissolving quickly.
C. It enhances the hydration of starch.
D. It interrupts gluten formation by coating flour particles.
cards.back: D. It interrupts gluten formation by coating flour particles.
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It interrupts gluten formation by coating flour particles.

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains the purpose of punching down dough after its initial fermentation in bread making?
A. To kill excess yeast and prevent over-fermentation
B. To increase the dough’s volume through added air
C. To enhance crust browning and accelerate proofing
D. To expel carbon dioxide, redistribute yeast, and develop gluten elasticity
cards.back: D. To expel carbon dioxide, redistribute yeast, and develop gluten elasticity
cards.rationale: Answer: D. To expel carbon dioxide, redistribute yeast, and develop gluten elasticity

cards.front:
In foam cakes like angel or chiffon cake, why is cream of tartar commonly added to beaten egg whites?
A. To sweeten the batter
B. To stabilize the foam structure during whipping
C. To enhance gluten development
D. To prevent coagulation of egg proteins
cards.back: B. To stabilize the foam structure during whipping
cards.rationale: Answer: B. To stabilize the foam structure during whipping

cards.front:
Why is the folding method essential in making sponge and angel food cakes?
A. Folding helps retain the air incorporated in beaten egg foams, maintaining cake volume.
B. Folding reduces fat clumping in the batter.
C. Folding incorporates more liquid into the batter to improve structure.
D. Folding dissolves sugar evenly throughout the batter.
cards.back: A. Folding helps retain the air incorporated in beaten egg foams, maintaining cake volume.
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Folding helps retain the air incorporated in beaten egg foams, maintaining cake volume.

cards.front:
Which mixing method for shortened cakes is best for achieving a tender crumb with fine texture and good volume?
A. Muffin Method – because it limits gluten development through minimal mixing
B. One-Bowl Method – because it uses all-purpose flour and mixes all ingredients quickly
C. Conventional Method – because it incorporates air through creaming and alternates dry and liquid ingredients
D. Sponge Method – because it separates eggs and beats whites to a foam before folding
cards.back: C. Conventional Method – because it incorporates air through creaming and alternates dry and liquid ingredients
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Conventional Method – because it incorporates air through creaming and alternates dry and liquid ingredients

cards.front:
Which of the following best describes the correct mixing sequence for preparing a chiffon cake?
A. Beat egg whites with sugar; mix egg yolks, oil, and liquid with dry ingredients; fold in the beaten egg whites.
B. Beat egg yolks with sugar; add oil and liquid; beat egg whites separately and mix everything at once.
C. Mix all dry ingredients; add whole eggs and oil; beat until smooth.
D. Beat egg whites and yolks together with sugar; add oil and liquid, then stir in dry ingredients.
cards.back: A. Beat egg whites with sugar; mix egg yolks, oil, and liquid with dry ingredients; fold in the beaten egg whites.
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Beat egg whites with sugar; mix egg yolks, oil, and liquid with dry ingredients; fold in the beaten egg whites.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements best explains why foam cakes are baked in ungreased pans and inverted during cooling?
A. Ungreased pans allow even heat distribution and inverting keeps the crust soft.
B. Greasing the pan adds moisture, and inverting traps steam.
C. Ungreased pans create a crusty exterior, and inverting enhances flavor.
D. Foam cakes need to cling to the sides of the pan during rising, and inverting prevents collapse while cooling
cards.back: D. Foam cakes need to cling to the sides of the pan during rising, and inverting prevents collapse while cooling
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Foam cakes need to cling to the sides of the pan during rising, and inverting prevents collapse while cooling

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains why cold water is essential when preparing pastry dough?
A. It evaporates quickly, helping in leavening
B. It activates gluten formation for better structure
C. It helps keep fat solid, promoting flakiness
D. It adds moisture for a chewy texture
cards.back: C. It helps keep fat solid, promoting flakiness
cards.rationale:
Answer:
C. It helps keep fat solid, promoting flakiness

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains why agar-agar can gel with raw pineapple, while gelatin cannot?
A. Agar-agar is a protein that resists enzymatic breakdown.
B. Agar-agar forms gels at higher temperatures than gelatin.
C. Agar-agar is a carbohydrate and is not affected by proteolytic enzymes like bromelin.
D. Agar-agar forms clearer gels, making it more stable with pineapple.
cards.back: C. Agar-agar is a carbohydrate and is not affected by proteolytic enzymes like bromelin.
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Agar-agar is a carbohydrate and is not affected by proteolytic enzymes like bromelin.

cards.front:
Why is agitation important during the freezing of ice cream?
A. It prevents sugar from concentrating
B. It equalizes salt and ice ratios in the mixture
C. It incorporates air and promotes the formation of small ice crystals
D. It raises the temperature inside the freezing can
cards.back: C. It incorporates air and promotes the formation of small ice crystals
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It incorporates air and promotes the formation of small ice crystals

cards.front:
Both coffee and tea are regarded as stimulating beverages. Which of the following best explains the physiological basis for this classification?
A. Both contain tannins, which directly stimulate brain activity.
B. They are brewed from roasted seeds and leaves, which increase metabolism regardless of content.
C. Their natural sugars provide an immediate energy boost that stimulates the body.
D. They contain caffeine, a central nervous system stimulant that enhances alertness and reduces fatigue
cards.back: D. They contain caffeine, a central nervous system stimulant that enhances alertness and reduces fatigue
cards.rationale: Answer: D. They contain caffeine, a central nervous system stimulant that enhances alertness and reduces fatigue

cards.front:
A roaster aims to create a balanced coffee blend that offers rich aroma, moderate acidity, and a slightly stronger caffeine kick without overpowering bitterness. Which blend composition is most appropriate?
A. 100% Arabica
B. 70% Arabica, 30% Robusta
C. 50% Arabica, 50% Liberica
D. 100% Robusta

Why is cocoa often mixed with sugar before adding to liquids during preparation?
A. To enhance the sweetness and chocolate flavor.
B. To prevent cocoa from forming lumps when mixed with liquid.
C. To reduce the bitterness of cocoa during boiling.
D. To allow the sugar to caramelize and thicken the drink.
cards.back: B. To prevent cocoa from forming lumps when mixed with liquid.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. To prevent cocoa from forming lumps when mixed with liquid.

cards.front:
What is the main principle in preparing both tea and coffee?
A. To dissolve all components including oils and tannins for full-bodied taste.
B. To extract the maximum amount of flavoring substances and minimal bitter tannins.
C. To always use boiling water for a stronger taste.
D. To add milk and sugar for balanced flavor.
cards.back: B. To extract the maximum amount of flavoring substances and minimal bitter tannins.
cards.rationale: Answer: B. To extract the maximum amount of flavoring substances and minimal bitter tannins.

cards.front:
Why should a teapot be scalded before brewing tea?
A. To sterilize the pot for food safety.
B. To prevent caffeine from reacting with metal.
C. To warm the pot and ensure optimal extraction of flavor compounds
D. To dissolve tannins and reduce bitterness.
cards.back: C. To warm the pot and ensure optimal extraction of flavor compounds
cards.rationale: Answer: C. To warm the pot and ensure optimal extraction of flavor compounds

cards.front:
A recipe calls for 1 tablespoon of coarse salt, but you only have fine salt. What principle should guide your adjustment?
A. Use the same amount, as salt type doesn’t affect salinity
B. Use more fine salt to match flavor intensity
C. Use less fine salt because it is denser and packs more per spoonful
D. Replace it with soy sauce for similar saltiness
cards.back: C. Use less fine salt because it is denser and packs more per spoonful
cards.rationale:
Answer:
C. Use less fine salt because it is denser and packs more per spoonful

cards.front:
What is the classification of tanglad (lemongrass) and siling labuyo (bird’s eye chili)?
A. Both are herbs because they are from plants and used for flavor
B. Tanglad is a spice, and siling labuyo is an herb because it is spicy
C. Tanglad is an herb, and siling labuyo is a spice because of the plant parts used
D. Both are spices because they are often used in stews and traditional recipes
cards.back: C. Tanglad is an herb, and siling labuyo is a spice because of the plant parts used
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Tanglad is an herb, and siling labuyo is a spice because of the plant parts used

cards.front:
Which seasoning would be most appropriate to reduce bitterness in a vegetable stir-fry without masking the natural flavors?
A. Soy sauce
B. Sugar
C. Vinegar
D. Salt

A chef finds that their stew is too salty. Which of the following is the most effective seasoning-related fix without diluting flavor too much?
A. Add more salt to mask the taste
B. Add vinegar or lemon juice
C. Add a sweet ingredient like honey
D. Add more water to dilute the salt
cards.back: B. Add vinegar or lemon juice
cards.rationale: Answer: B. Add vinegar or lemon juice

cards.front:
You are preparing a dry rub for grilling meat. Which of the following ingredient combinations contributes best to flavor penetration and surface browning?
A. Garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar
B. Salt, black pepper, lemon juice, vinegar
C. Soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, honey
D. Salt, black pepper, lemon juice, olive oil
cards.back: A. Garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar
cards.rationale: Answer: A. Garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar

cards.front:
Why is salt often used first in marinating meat, even when acidic ingredients like vinegar or citrus juice are also present?
A. It enhances sweetness
B. It tenderizes proteins chemically
C. It draws moisture out to dehydrate meat
D. It helps seasonings penetrate by breaking down the protein structure
cards.back: D. It helps seasonings penetrate by breaking down the protein structure
cards.rationale: Answer: D. It helps seasonings penetrate by breaking down the protein structure

cards.front:
Why is an acid rinse effective in preventing browning of peeled fruits and vegetables?
A. It removes surface moisture that causes browning
B. It inhibits oxygen penetration by tightening cell walls
C. It lowers pH, slowing down enzymatic activity
D. It denatures surface proteins preventing browning
cards.back: C. It lowers pH, slowing down enzymatic activity
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It lowers pH, slowing down enzymatic activity

cards.front:
What is the primary functional reason for basting during roasting?
A. It prevents microbial growth on the surface
B. It caramelizes sugars for deeper browning
C. It adds moisture and prevents surface drying
D. It enhances the speed of protein coagulation
cards.back: C. It adds moisture and prevents surface drying
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It adds moisture and prevents surface drying

cards.front:
Why is blanching used before freezing vegetables like broccoli or green beans?
A. To inactivate enzymes that cause spoilage
B. To cook them halfway before final use
C. To improve their color by increasing chlorophyll
D. To reduce their carbohydrate content during long-term storage.
cards.back: A. To inactivate enzymes that cause spoilage
cards.rationale: Answer: A. To inactivate enzymes that cause spoilage

cards.front:
During caramelization, which chemical change primarily contributes to the flavor development?
A. Protein denaturation
B. Lipid oxidation
C. Maillard reaction
D. Thermal degradation of sugar molecules
cards.back: D. Thermal degradation of sugar molecules
cards.rationale: Answer: D. Thermal degradation of sugar molecules

cards.front:
What is the primary reason clarified butter (drawn butter) is preferred for high-heat cooking like sautéing or frying?
A. It is less expensive than regular butter
B. It contains more saturated fat
C. It has a higher smoke point due to removed milk solids
D. It is thicker and coats foods better
cards.back: C. It has a higher smoke point due to removed milk solids
cards.rationale: Answer: C. It has a higher smoke point due to removed milk solids

cards.front:
Which seasoning would be most appropriate to reduce bitterness in a vegetable stir-fry without masking the natural flavors?
A. Soy sauce
B. Vinegar
C. Sugar
D. Salt

A recipe calls for 2 liters of broth. You only have a standard US measuring cup on hand. Approximately how many full cups will you need to measure out 2 liters of broth?
A. 6 cups
B. 8 cups
C. 9 cups
D. 12 cups

You are preparing a recipe that requires 1.5 pounds of flour, but your kitchen scale only measures in grams. Approximately how many grams of flour should you use?
A. 500 grams
B. 680 grams
C. 750 grams
D. 900 grams

Why does deep-frying cook food faster than baking at the same temperature (e.g., 180°C or 350°F)?
A. Oil conducts heat more slowly than air
B. Oil radiates heat more intensely than air
C. Oil has a higher heat transfer coefficient than air
D. Air circulates more efficiently than oil
cards.back: C. Oil has a higher heat transfer coefficient than air
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Oil has a higher heat transfer coefficient than air

cards.front:
In which cooking method does radiation play the dominant role in transferring heat directly to the surface of the food?
A. Simmering
B. Broiling
C. Steaming D. Braising

Why is moist-heat cooking generally preferred for tough cuts of meat like beef brisket or pork shoulder?
A. It enhances the Maillard reaction for better browning
B. It breaks down connective tissues into gelatin through slow, wet cooking
C. It retains less moisture, making meat easier to shred
D. It crisps the outer surface for added texture
cards.back: B. It breaks down connective tissues into gelatin through slow, wet cooking
cards.rationale: Answer: B. It breaks down connective tissues into gelatin through slow, wet cooking

cards.front:
Which of the following best explains the distinction between spices and herbs in culinary use?
A. Spices are always stronger in flavor and must be used in larger quantities
B. Herbs are derived from dried roots while spices come from stems
C. Herbs are primarily leafy and used fresh or dried; spices come from other plant parts like seeds and bark
D. There is no clear difference; both terms are interchangeable in recipes
cards.back: C. Herbs are primarily leafy and used fresh or dried; spices come from other plant parts like seeds and bark
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Herbs are primarily leafy and used fresh or dried; spices come from other plant parts like seeds and bark

cards.front:
Why is pork belly barbecue generally more tender and juicy than tenderloin barbecue, even though tenderloin is a leaner and more tender cut?
A. Pork belly has less connective tissue, making it easier to cook
B. Tenderloin retains more moisture due to its low fat content
C. Pork belly has higher fat content that melts during cooking, adding moisture and flavor
D. Tenderloin absorbs more marinade, making it taste richer and juicier
cards.back: C. Pork belly has higher fat content that melts during cooking, adding moisture and flavor
cards.rationale: Answer: C. Pork belly has higher fat content that melts during cooking, adding moisture and flavor

cards.front:
What is the best way to stabilize whipped cream for longer storage?
A. Add cornstarch

A young man with bipolar disorder is admitted to telemetry. His cardiologist prescribes a low sodium diet. You would need to be concerned with a food and drug interaction if the patient’s medications included which one of the following*

a. Lithium
b. Elavil
c. Parnate
d. Zoloft

Chemotherapy that includes antimetabolites, such as methotrexate, can reduce the availability of which one of the following vitamins?*

a. Vitamin A
b. Vitamin K
c. Folic acid
d. Pyridoxine

When counselling a patient who is starting on the medication isoniazid, the die titian would need to be concerned if the patient’s intake of which of the following is inadequate?*

a. Vitamin A
b. Vitamin K
c. Folic acid
d. Pyridoxine

A client with blood clotting disorder is starting on an anticoagulant. The die titian should be concerned if the client reports use of which of the following herbs?*

a. St John’s Wort
b. Echinacea
c. Garlic
d. Chromium picolinate

Which of the following have the greatest risk of serious side effects if used inappropriately?*

a. Herbs
b. Dietary supplements
c. Over-the-counter medications
d. Prescription medications

Patients on corticosteroid therapy may benefit from supplementation of*

a. Vitamin A
b. Vitamin B
c. Vitamin C
d. Arginine

Over-the-counter medications:*

a. Altered food intake
b. Are often used for longer periods than prescription medications
c. Are unlikely to react with prescription medications
d. May be used for the wrong reasons and in the wrong amounts
cards.back: d. May be used for the wrong reasons and in the wrong amounts
cards.rationale: Answer: d. May be used for the wrong reasons and in the wrong amounts
options: Are often used for longer periods than prescription medications
Are unlikely to react with prescription medications
May be used for the wrong reasons and in the wrong amounts

cards.front:
Side effects of drugs may include:*

a. Altered food intake
b. Altered absorption, metabolism and excretion of nutrients
c. Altered absorption, metabolism and excretion of drugs
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above
options: Altered absorption, metabolism and excretion of nutrients
Altered absorption, metabolism and excretion of drugs

cards.front:
Who is more at risk from protein calorie malnutrition?*

a. A cancer patient in chemotherapy
b. A patient with gastric ulcer
c. A patient with Chron’s disease
d. A patient with megaloblastic anemia
cards.back: a. A cancer patient in chemotherapy
cards.rationale: Answer: a. A cancer patient in chemotherapy

cards.front:
Mucosal effects of drugs on nutrients absorption include:*

a. Damage to mucosal cell
b. Alteration of pH
c. Inactivation of enzyme system
d. A and C
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Damage to mucosal cell

cards.front:
Alcohol’s primary effect on nutrition is to:*

a. Stimulate the appetite
b. Alter taste sensitivity
c. Depress the appetite
d. Induce nausea and vomiting

Mineral oil is safe to use as regular laxative since it does not adversely affect nutrition*

a. True
b. False

When drug binds to a nutrient:*

a. The nutrient is better absorbed
b. Both are excreted in the urine
c. The drug is better absorbed
d. There is no effect on nutrition
cards.back: b. Both are excreted in the urine
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Both are excreted in the urine
options: Both are excreted in the urine
There is no effect on nutrition

cards.front:
Guidelines for administering drugs to someone receiving a tube feeding*

a. Give medication orally whenever possible
b. Give medication in the form of pills versus liquid
c. Consider giving the drug for injection
d. A and b
e. A and c
cards.back: a. Give medication orally whenever possible
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Give medication orally whenever possible
options: Give medication in the form of pills versus liquid
Consider giving the drug for injection

cards.front:
The elderly population is at high risk for developing problems related to nutrition and drug therapy because:*

a. They are often malnourished
b. They frequently take several drugs for long periods of time
c. They have very high nutrient requirements
d. A and b
cards.back: b. They frequently take several drugs for long periods of time
cards.rationale: Answer: b. They frequently take several drugs for long periods of time
options: They frequently take several drugs for long periods of time
They have very high nutrient requirements

cards.front:
Some antacids contribute significant amount of*

a. Calcium
b. Phosphorus
c. Sodium
d. A and c

Drugs which are degraded by high acidityshould be taken:*

a. Along with a meal
b. One-half hour before a meal
c. Two or three hours after a meal
d. B and c
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Along with a meal
options: Two or three hours after a meal

cards.front:
Drugs which are negatively affected by a low stomach pH should be taken with meals.*

a. True
b. False

Aspirin given on full stomach works faster than when it is given on an empty stomach*

a. True
b. False

Giving drugs along with meals may help to alleviate the problems of:*

a. Inflammation of the mouth
b. Alterations in smell
c. Nausea
d. Alterations in taste

All of the following should not be taken along with tetracycline except:*

a. Dairy products
b. Fruit juices
c. Antacids the contains calcium
d. Iron supplement

Iatrogenic malnutrition is:*

a. Vitamin, mineral malabsorption
b. Protein malabsorption
c. Protein, calorie malnutrition
d. Kwashiorkor

A 25-year-old male with a brain tumor has had chemotheraphy and is now neutropenic. Which of the following should be acceptable for him to consume?*

a. Fresh roasted peanuts and lemon-lime soda
b. Cottage cheese and fresh fruit
c. Homemade coleslaw and crackers
d. Well-done hamburger and French fries
cards.back: d. Well-done hamburger and French fries
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Well-done hamburger and French fries
options: Fresh roasted peanuts and lemon-lime soda

cards.front:
When assessing the nutritional status of a patient who has received radiation therapy, which of the following is the least useful parameter?*

a. Total lymphocyte count
b. Percentage of usual body weight
c. Four-day intake record
d. Gastrointestinal symptoms

Cancer patients who have failed to maintain nutritional status by oral intake should receive:*

a. Additional written materials to manage their choices
b. An enteral tube
c. Peripheral parenteral nutrition
d. Total parenteral nutrition
options: Additional written materials to manage their choices

cards.front:
The cancer cachexia syndrome is characterized by:*

a. Muscle wasting
b. Weight loss
c. Anorexia
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
Factors that contribute to anorexia and poor food intake in people with cancer may include:*

a. A tumor obstructing the GI tract
b. Lack of energy to prepare meals
c. Psychological stress and pain
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above
options: A tumor obstructing the GI tract
Lack of energy to prepare meals

cards.front:
Side effect of chemotherapy or radiation therapy that affect food intake include all except:*

a. Stomatitis
b. Mouth blindness
c. Nausea and vomiting
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
People with cancer who receive radiation therapy to the head and neck often develop:*

a. Increase saliva production
b. Mouth ulcers
c. Altered taste perception
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
Food aversions can be minimized in people undergoing chemotherapy by:*

a. Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods when they are feeling sick
b. Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods within an hour of treatments
c. Reminding them not to eat within an hour or two before or after treatments
d. A and b
cards.back: a. Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods when they are feeling sick
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods when they are feeling sick
options: Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods when they are feeling sick
Encouraging them to eat only their favourite foods within an hour of treatments
Reminding them not to eat within an hour or two before or after treatments

cards.front:
Which kind of dietary fat is most implicated in cancer causation?*

a. Omega – 3 fatty acid
b. Monounsaturated fats
c. Polyunsaturated vegetable oils
d. None of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. None of the above

cards.front:
Cancers of the head and neck correlate best to:*

a. Fiber intake
b. Alcohol intake and tobacco use
c. Fat intake
d. None of the above
cards.back: b. Alcohol intake and tobacco use
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Alcohol intake and tobacco use

cards.front:
To compensate for weight loss during cancer treatments, clients should be encouraged to:*

a. Eat extra food immediately before treatment
b. Ext extra food immediately after treatment
c. Eat extra food between treatments
d. A and b
cards.back: c. Eat extra food between treatments
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Eat extra food between treatments
options: Eat extra food immediately before treatment
Ext extra food immediately after treatment

cards.front:
Enteral and parenteral nutrition should be used only after the cancer client:*

a. Has become severely depleted
b. Has lost significant amount of weight
c. Is on some type of anticancer therapy
d. A and B
options: Has lost significant amount of weight
Is on some type of anticancer therapy

cards.front:
Cancer clients who complaint of fullness should be told to*

a. Eat less frequently
b. Consume liquids with meals
c. Eat only three meal per day
d. Avoid high fat foods
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Avoid high fat foods
options: Eat only three meal per day

cards.front:
Common causes of anorexia in cancer clients include all of the following except:*

a. Psychological stresses
b. A premature feeling of fullness
c. Decreased absorption of nutrients
d. The pain associated with a tumor
cards.back: d. The pain associated with a tumor
cards.rationale: Answer: d. The pain associated with a tumor
options: The pain associated with a tumor

cards.front:
A Dietitian in a dialysis clinic should recommend oral consumption of vitamin in an amount greater than the DRI?*

a. Folic acid
b. Vitamin B12
c. Vitamin D
d. Vitamin A

A hemodialysis patient has labs drawn prior to receiving his regular treatment which reveal a BUN of 105 mg/dl and serum sodium of 128 mEqL. He has also gained 5.0 kg since his previous treatment. What would have caused this?*

a. Excessive intake of fluid and protein, inadequate intake of sodium
b. Excessive intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
c. Inadequate intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
d. Inadequate intake of fluid and sodium, excessive intake of protein
cards.back: b. Excessive intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Excessive intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
options: Excessive intake of fluid and protein, inadequate intake of sodium
Excessive intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
Inadequate intake of fluid, protein, and sodium
Inadequate intake of fluid and sodium, excessive intake of protein

cards.front:
Clients with advanced kidney disease frequently develop renal osteodystrophy. This is related to a lack of which of the following?*

a. Phosphate
b. Calciferol
c. Calcitriol
d. Parathyroid hormone

The lab results for a peritoneal dialysis patient reveal a phosphorus level of 9.5 mg/dl. The patient reports taking a phosphate binder
with meals and snack. The RD’s first step should be to:*

a. Counsel the patient about decreasing phosphorus intake
b. Counsel the patient about increasing phosphorus intake
c. Recommend a higher dosage of the phosphate binder
d. Determine the current prescribed medication dosage
cards.back: d. Determine the current prescribed medication dosage
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Determine the current prescribed medication dosage
options: Counsel the patient about decreasing phosphorus intake
Counsel the patient about increasing phosphorus intake
Recommend a higher dosage of the phosphate binder
Determine the current prescribed medication dosage

cards.front:
For the treatment of which condition would a “high alkaline ash” diet be recommended?*

a. Struvite stones
b. Uric acid stones
c. Hyperoxaluria
d. Hyperparathyroidism

After review of his lab work, a patient was informed that his renal failure had progressed to the point where he now needed dialysis treatment. Which lab results would have indicated this?*

a. Hyperkalemia
b. Elevated GFR
c. Low GFR
d. Hypokalemia

Urea excretion is related to ________, while creatinine excretion is related to________.*

a. Muscle mass, protein intake
b. Protein intake, muscle mass
c. Protein intake, adipose reserves
d. Protein intake, calcium intake
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Protein intake, muscle mass

cards.front:
All of the following represent functions of the kidney except:*

a. Maintenance of fluid and electrolyte balance
b. Inactivation of vitamin D
c. Elimination of metabolic waste products
d. Maintenance of acid-base balance
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Inactivation of vitamin D
options: Maintenance of fluid and electrolyte balance

cards.front:
The normal glomerular filtration rate is:*

a. 50-90 ml/min
b. 70-100 ml/min
c. 90-120 ml/min
d. 110-140 ml.min

When a renal client is retaining sodium and fluid:*

a. Body weight will decrease
b. Blood pressure will increase
c. Urine output will decrease
d. A and C
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Blood pressure will increase

cards.front:
To estimate daily fluid needs of a renal client, add ________ millilitres to the 24 hr urine output.*

a. 200
b. 300
c. 400
d. 500

An acid ash would be created by:*

a. Corn, cranberries
b. Milk
c. Vegetables
d. Fruits

Symptoms of nephrosis include:*

a. Dehydration, hypocholesterolemia
b. Albuminuria, hypercholesterolemia
c. Edema, hypocholesterolemia
d. Hypotension, hyperalbuminuria

When a renal client is retaining sodium and fluids*

a. Body weight will decrease
b. Blood pressure will increase
c. Urine output will decrease
d. A and C
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Blood pressure will increase

cards.front:
Foods considered part of the fluid allowance in a renal diet include all of the following except:*

a. Vegetable high in water content
b. Popsicles
c. Ice cream
d. Jello
cards.back: a. Vegetable high in water content
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Vegetable high in water content

cards.front:
Bone disease is a frequent complication of chronic renal failure.*

a. True
b. False

Renal failure diets are intentionally low in all of the following except*

a. Phosphorus
b. Protein
c. Calcium
d. Sodium

Aluminium-containing antacids are sometimes given to renal failure clients to:*

a. Decrease phosphorus intake
b. Decrease absorption of phosphorus
c. Bind phosphorus in the GI tract
d. B and C
options: Bind phosphorus in the GI tract

cards.front:
Anemia unrelated to iron deficiency may occur in chronic renal failure due to:*

a. Decrease production of erythropoietin
b. Increased synthesis of red blood cells
c. Increased life span of red blood cells
d. A and c
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Decrease production of erythropoietin
options: Increased synthesis of red blood cells
Increased life span of red blood cells

cards.front:
Corticosteroids given after renal transplants can result in all of the following except:*

a. Negative nitrogen balance
b. Edema
c. Excessive weight loss
d. Glucose intolerance

The kidney plays an essential role in which of the following:*

a. Epinephrine synthesis
b. Erythropoietin synthesis
c. Converting vitamin A to its active form
d. Breaking down red blood cells
options: Converting vitamin A to its active form

cards.front:
Metabolic changes that occur in renal failure include:*
a. GFR increases
b. BUN increases
c. Blood uric acid levels increase
d. B an C only
cards.rationale: Answer: d. B an C only

cards.front:
Symptoms of Uremia include*

a. Hyperactivity
b. Unpleasant taste in the mouth
c. Diminished mental alertness
d. B and C

Objective(s) of dietary management of chronic renal failure include:*

a. To maintain negative nitrogen balance
b. To delay the progression of renal failure
c. To prevent bone disease
d. B and C
options: To delay the progression of renal failure

cards.front:
Once a client with chronic renal failure begins dialysis, the protein content of their diet should be:*

a. Increase
b. Decrease
c. Stay the same
d. Be eliminated

Which of the following nutrients generally restricted in the diet of a client with renal failure?*

a. Vitamin D
b. Zinc
c. Potassium
d. Vitamin B6

Renal disease often contributes to which of the following medical condition(s):*

a. Anemia
b. Bone disease
c. Hypercalcemia
d. A and B

Clients with renal failure usually require supplement of which nutrient(s)?*

a. Calcium
b. Vitamin D
c. Vitamin B6
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
Strategies for controlling fluid intake include:*

a. Chew gum and Eat ice
b. Suck on hard candy
c. Gargle with refrigerated mouthwash
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
Acute renal failure is most likely to develop in response to which of the following:*

a. Atherosclerosis
b. Severe blood loss after trauma
c. Hypertension
d. Diabetes
cards.back: b. Severe blood loss after trauma
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Severe blood loss after trauma

cards.front:
A hypercatabolic state complicates acute renal failure because*

a. Protein is broken down for energy, causing blood urea to rise
b. Protein is broken down for energy, causing blood potassium to rise
c. The client usually feels too sick to eat, so consumes too few calories
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above
options: Protein is broken down for energy, causing blood urea to rise
Protein is broken down for energy, causing blood potassium to rise
The client usually feels too sick to eat, so consumes too few calories

cards.front:
The dietary management of nephrotic syndrome includes:*

a. Restricting calories
b. Consuming high levels of protein
c. Consuming generous amount of sodium
d. Consuming foods that reduce serum lipids
cards.back: b. Consuming high levels of protein
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Consuming high levels of protein
options: Consuming foods that reduce serum lipids

cards.front:
Sources of water do not include:*

a. Water itself
b. Foods
c. Metabolic reactions
d. Minerals

Dialysis reduces all of the following symptoms except:*

a. Uremia
b. Edema
c. Hypertension
d. Anemia

Individuals who are not generally considered as candidates for kidney transplants include all of the following except:*

a. They are very old
b. Those with other life-threatening conditions
c. Children
d. Those who prefer dialysis

Recent research indicates that the addition of keto acids to a low protein diet increases the rate of renal deterioration.*

a. True
b. False

Once dialysis is initiated protein intake:*

a. Is less restrictive
b. Is more restrictive
c. Remains the same
d. Emphasizes the addition of non-essential amino acid sources
options: Emphasizes the addition of non-essential amino acid sources

cards.front:
Acute renal failure is frequently caused by problems that originate outside of the kidney.*

a. True
b. False

Kidney disease cannot be caused by:*

a. Consumption of toxic metals
b. Habitual consumption of water
c. Consumption of a diet habitually high in protein
d. Trauma
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Habitual consumption of water
options: Consumption of a diet habitually high in protein

cards.front:
Kilocalories usually need to be increased in protein-restricted diet because an adequate kilocalorie intake____________________.*

a. Assists in control of serum potassium
b. Is necessary to prevent the renal anemia
c. Controls and prevents osteodystrophy
d. Spares protein
options: Assists in control of serum potassium
Is necessary to prevent the renal anemia

cards.front:
Compared with renal failure patients who are not on dialysis, patients on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis require:*

a. The same amount of dietary protein
b. Less dietary protein
c. More dietary protein
d. A different kind of protein
options: The same amount of dietary protein

cards.front:
Which of the following would be a good snack for a patient with acute renal failure who is not on dialysis?*

a. Hard candy
b. Cheese
c. Milk
d. Oranges

Some renal patients need to avoid salt substitutes because these often contain:*

a. Phosphorus
b. Potassium
c. Protein
d. Calcium

The _________intake from food is not monitored in renal patients.*

a. Vitamin D
b. Fluid
c. Protein
d. Sodium

Which of the following are high in potassium?*

a. Grapes
b. Cranberry juice
c. Baked potatoes
d. Canned pears

The most important nutritional consideration in treating patients with kidney stones is to:*

a. Limit calcium intake
b. Restrict all end products of protein metabolism
c. Restrict all food sources of calcium, oxalic acid,
and prunes
d. Increase fluid intake
options: Restrict all end products of protein metabolism
Restrict all food sources of calcium, oxalic acid,

cards.front:
A patient with Type 1 diabetes presents to the emergency room with dehydration and Kussmaul respirations. Urinalysis reveals ketonuria; lab results show blood glucose of 525 and pCO2 of 59.This patient is experiencing*

a. Respiratory acidosis
b. Respiratory alkalosis
c. Metabolic acidocis
d. Metabolic alkalosis

A chronic COPD patient with carbon dioxide retention would have which one of the following acid-base imbalances?*

a. Respiratory acidosis
b. Respiratory alkalosis
c. Metabolic acidosis
d. Metabolic alkalosis

When pCO2 is 28, bicarbonate is 32, and pH is > 7.45, how do the kidneys compensate to assure acid-base balance?*

a. Conserve bicarbonate
b. Conserve sodium ions
c. Excrete bicarbonate
d. Conserve carbon dioxide

Which of the following nutrition measures is most important for the person with acute respiratory failure*

a. High volumes of fluids pr electrolytes to clean the lungs of fluids
b. A diet prescription that is low in carbohydrate and high in fat than a typical diet following acute stress
c. Attention to ensuring an adequate but not excessive energy intake
d. A high kilocalorie, high protein diet to support wearing from mechanical ventilation
cards.back: b. A diet prescription that is low in carbohydrate and high in fat than a typical diet following acute stress
cards.rationale: Answer: b. A diet prescription that is low in carbohydrate and high in fat than a typical diet following acute stress
options: High volumes of fluids pr electrolytes to clean the lungs of fluids
A diet prescription that is low in carbohydrate and high in fat than a typical diet following acute stress
Attention to ensuring an adequate but not excessive energy intake
A high kilocalorie, high protein diet to support wearing from mechanical ventilation

cards.front:
Factors that frequently contribute in wasting the patients with COPD include*

a. Anorexia, medications and respiratory infections
b. Dehydration, fat malabsorption and lactose intolerance
c. Essential fatty acids deficiencies and potassium imbalances
d. Vitamin K deficiencies, dysphagia and low fiber,low potassium diets
cards.back: a. Anorexia, medications and respiratory infections
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Anorexia, medications and respiratory infections
options: Dehydration, fat malabsorption and lactose intolerance
Essential fatty acids deficiencies and potassium imbalances
Vitamin K deficiencies, dysphagia and low fiber,low potassium diets

cards.front:
A 60 year old male is diagnosed as having acute respiratory failure, and is incubated and placed on a mechanical ventilator. He is  maintained with TPN. The solution used should:*

a. be high in glucose
b. be low in phosphorus
c. provide half of the non-protein kcal from fat
d. provide 3.0 grams of protein/ kg per Dayton
cards.back: c. provide half of the non-protein kcal from fat
cards.rationale: Answer: c. provide half of the non-protein kcal from fat
options: provide half of the non-protein kcal from fat
provide 3.0 grams of protein/ kg per Dayton

cards.front:
The underlying pathological processes in cardiovascular disease are:*

a. Atherosclerosis and hypertension
b. Coronary occlusion and obesity
c. Diabetes mellitus and cerebrovascular accidental
d. Kidney failure and congestive heart failure
options: Kidney failure and congestive heart failure

cards.front:
The first action a hypertensive patient should take to lower blood pressure is to:*

a. Restrict fluid to 1500 milliliters per day at
b. Eliminate saturated fat from the diet
c. Lose weight if necessary
d. Limit sodium Intake to 1 gram per day
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Lose weight if necessary
options: Restrict fluid to 1500 milliliters per day at
Eliminate saturated fat from the diet
Limit sodium Intake to 1 gram per day

cards.front:
The carriers of cholesterol to the cells for storage are the*

a. Chylomicrons
b. High-density lipoproteins
c. Low-density lipoproteins
d. Very low-density lipoproteins

Monounsaturated fats may help lower blood cholesterol levels. Which of the following are mono unsaturated:*

a. Safflower and soybean oils
b. Canola and peanut oils
c. Sunflower seed and cottonseed oils
d. Olive and corn oils
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Canola and peanut oils

cards.front:
Soluble fiber also helps to lower blood cholesterol levels. Which of the following are good sources of soluble fiber?*

a. Broccoli and prunes
b. Whole-wheat bread and grapes
c. Green beans and raspberries
d. Oats and legumes

Omega-3 fatty acids contribute to cardiovascular health by lowering triglyceride levels and reducing platelet aggregation. Good sources of these fatty acids are:*

a. Lobster, bass and oyster
b. Catfish, shrimp and clams
c. Perch, walleye and pike
d. Herring, salmon and tuna
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Herring, salmon and tuna

cards.front:
Products labeled “very low sodium” must contain less than _____ milligrams of sodium per serving*

a. 20
b. 35
c. 50
d. 65

The obese person is at increased risk of cardiovascular disease if the excess fat is concentrated in the:*

a. Abdominal area
b. Hips and thighs
c. Extremities
d. Buttocks

A high sucrose intake is related to cardiovascular disease because:*

a. Many cardiac patients have a genetic deficiency of sucrose
b. A high-sugar diet causes hyperactivity and hypertension
c. Excess sugar has to be excreted, causing premature aging of the kidney
d. Sucrose stimulates triglyceride production by the body
cards.back: d. Sucrose stimulates triglyceride production by the body
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Sucrose stimulates triglyceride production by the body
options: Many cardiac patients have a genetic deficiency of sucrose
A high-sugar diet causes hyperactivity and hypertension
Excess sugar has to be excreted, causing premature aging of the kidney
Sucrose stimulates triglyceride production by the body

cards.front:
Which of the following is not always a nutritional goal for a child with renal disease?*

a. Promote normal growth and development
b. Maintain current hydration status
c. Minimize uremic toxicity
d. Stimulate patient well-being
cards.back: a. Promote normal growth and development
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Promote normal growth and development

cards.front:
The risk of heart disease is reduced in people who have high blood levels of*

a. Triglyceride
b. very low-density lipoprotein
c. low-density lipoproteins
d. high-density lipoproteins

Fatty acids with a double bond at one part of the molecule are referred to as*

a. Monounsaturated
b. Hydrogenated
c. Saturated
d. essential

a. Hg in the canned food product
b. Al residue in the processed food product

cards.rationale: Answer: b. Al residue in the processed food product
options: Hg in the canned food product
Al residue in the processed food product
Nitrates and nitrites in the processed food product

cards.front:
The more common microorganism that is involved in alcoholic fermentation is*

a. Acetobacter xylinum
b. Acetobacter aceti
c. Sacccharomyces cerevisiae
d. Saccharomyces carlsbergensis

The oxygen requirement in acetic fermentation is*

a. aerobic
b. anaerobic
c. Facultative
d. Microaerophilic

Type of microorganism that will grow in strawberry jam*

a. halophilic
b. xerophilic
c. thermophilic
d. osmophilic

Pasteurization is applied in processing*

a. high acid foods
b. alkaline foods
c. low acid foods
d. salty foods

The process of passing steam over canned food before sealing is*

a. blanching
b. exhausting
c. sulfiting
d. Steaming

Sentence A. Volatile nutrients are easily lost during drying.
Sentence B. Vitamins A and C are volatile nutrients.*

a. Sentence A is correct.
b. Sentence B is correct.
c. Both sentences are correct.
d. Both sentences are incorrect.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Both sentences are correct.
options: Volatile nutrients are easily lost during drying.
Vitamins A and C are volatile nutrients.*

cards.front:
Sentence A. Fresh green salads maybe contaminated with coliforms.
Sentence B. This type of contamination is biological.*

a. Sentence A is correct.
