b. 12 kg
c. 15 kg
d. 14 kg

Characterized by edema except: *
a. HPN
b. CHF
c, a & b only
d. severe protein deficiency

Anthropometric measurement/s that may be used in equations to estimate the stature of non-ambulatory persons: *
a. calf circumference
b. knee height
c. all of the above
d. midarm circumference

The best diet for a child with phenylketonuria: *
a. none of the above
b. low phenylalanine & methionine
c. low phenylalanine & tyrosine
d. low phenylalanine

Conditions that are contraindicated for the use of tube feeding except: *
a. paralytic ileus
b. peritonitis
c. metabolic stress
d. intractable vomiting

Food products avoided in celiac disease: *
a. those made from corn or millet
b. those made from wheat or barley
c. those with high fat content
d. those with lactose
cards.back: b. those made from wheat or barley
cards.rationale: Answer: b. those made from wheat or barley

cards.front:
Diabetes mellitus characterized by absolute insulin deficiency: *
a. prediabetes
b. GDM
c. type 2 DM
d. Type 1 DM

The accepted total cholesterol to HDL ratio is: *
a. 6.5
b. 5.5
c. 4.5
d. 4.0

Primary causes of peptic ulcer except: *
a. spicy foods
b. gastritis
c. aspirins & other NSAIDs
d. pylori infection

The best protein allowance for severely malnourished children is: *
a. 2-3 g/kg DBW
b. 4-5 g/kg DBW
c. 3-4 g/kg DBW
d. none of the above

This medication can produce severe malabsorption: *
a. laxatives
b. aspirin
c. diuretics
d. cough syrup

This hormone decreases the urge to eat and increases physical activity to produce a negative energy balance. *
a. leptin
b. ghrelin
c. adiponectin
d. insulin

A prolonged use of corticosteroids can lead to: *
a. Na retention
b. fatty liver
c. increased protein catabolism
d. poor glucose tolerance

The molecule most directly linked to the initiation of atherosclerotic plaques is: *
a. thromoxane A2
b. tumor necrosis factor
c. platelet derived growth factor
d. oxidized cholesterol

Medications that reduce stomach acidity can impair the absorption of: *
a. B12, folate, and Fe
b. Na & K
c. thiamin & riboflavin
d. fat-soluble vitamins
cards.rationale: Answer: a. B12, folate, and Fe

cards.front:
Type of formula delivery that is administered slowly and in constant amount over a period of 8 hours or 24 hours: *
a. drip
b. continuous
c. cyclic
d. intermittent

It must be supplemented in glycogen storage disease: *
a. iron
b. calcium
c. vitamin K
d. potassium

A patient was put on a low-fat, low-cholesterol diet for a heart condition. He was asked to stay away butter and lard. What type of fat can be used for cooking? *
a. coconut oil
b. soya oil
c. shortening
d. palm oil

A metabolic change that accompanies acute stress is: *
a. hypoglycemia
b. muscle protein catabolism
c. elevated immune response
d. reduced heart & respiratory rates

Vitamin K deficiency is frequently drug-induced. Which of the following drugs might be associated with this deficiency? 1. antibiotics 2. mineral oil 3. diuretics 4. anticoagulants *
a. 1 & 2 only
b. 1, 3, 4 only
c. 1, 2, 3 only
d. 1, 2, 4 only

A dialysis patient was prescribed 55g of protein per day. The amount of HBV protein should be at least: *
a. 66g
b. 33g
c. 41g
d. 39g

Foods with low glycemic index except: *
a. strawberry jam
b. rice noodles
c. legumes
d. boiled potatoes
cards.rationale: Answer: d. boiled potatoes

cards.front:
A digestible meal of several food items contains 70 g CHO, 25 g Fat, 20 g PRO and 45 g alcohol. Assuming 100% of this food energy can be utilized, calculate the approximate total yield of energy. *
a. 640 kcal
b. 815 kcal
c. 900 kcal
d. 990 kcal

Dietary recommendation/s for patients with nephritic syndrome: *
a. Ca & K restriction
b. a high protein intake
c. Na restriction
d. fluid restriction

It is the surgical creation of an opening from the body surface to the intestinal tract to allow defecation: *
a. ileostomy
b. enterocutaneous fistula
c. stoma
d. fistula

The nutrition therapy usually prescribed for a patient with heart failure: *
a. total fat intake reduction
b. weight loss
c. sodium restriction
d. cholesterol restriction

It contributes to impaired mucosal resistance in gastric ulcer: *
a. milk
b. bread
c. orange juice
d. caffeine

Reabsorption of Na in the distal and collecting tubules causes: *
a. decreased water reabsorption
b. secretion of PTH
c. lowering of the GFR
d. expansion of blood volume
cards.back: d. expansion of blood volume
cards.rationale: Answer: d. expansion of blood volume

cards.front:
Defects in lipid metabolism can be due to: *
a. specific organ failure
b. endocrinopathy
c. inborn error of metabolism d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
The primary risk factor in cases of fatty liver that is not related to excessive alcohol intake is: *
a. a high-protein diet
b. insulin resistance
c. use of illicit drugs
d. a high-fat diet

During the initial phase of physical exercise for non-diabetics and individuals with well-controlled diabetes, what is the primary source of fuel? *
a. blood glucose
b. muscle glycogen
c. free fatty acids
d. amino acids

Most possible cause of diarrhea among tube-fed patients is: *
a. rapid delivery of formula
b. bacterial contamination
c. lactose intolerance
d. drug therapy

If a patient is to restrict phosphorus intake, which nutrient may be unintentionally restricted?
a. K
b. H2O
c. Ca
d. Na

Refeeding syndrome can bring about a dangerous fluctuation in: *
a. serum liver enzyme levels
b. ketone bodies
c. blood triglyceride levels
d. serum electrolytes

A nonsurgical approach to gallstone treatment is: *
a. weight loss
b. cholecystectomy
c. immunosuppressive drug therapy
d. dissolution & fragmentation

A diet that excludes all animal foods (meat, poultry, fish, egg, dairy products) is called: *
a. macrobiotic diet
b. plant-based diet
c. vegan diet
d. lactovegetarian diet

Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs suppress inflammatory processes by: *
a. inhibiting eicosanoid synthesis
b. interfering with histamine secretion
c. impairing the actions of certain cytokines
d. inhibiting the absorption of omega-6 fatty acid

After an injury, the following changes occur in the damaged tissue except: *
a. reduced capillary permeability
b. warmth
c. fluid accumulation
d. increased blood flow

A very common cause of chronic kidney disease is: *
a. exposure to toxins
b. diabetes mellitus
c. autoimmune disease
d. HPN

How many grams of carbohydrate would be contained in 2000ml of blenderized formula with a caloric density of 1.5kcal/ml, 65% of which are from carbohydrate? *
a. 396 g
b. 483 g
c. 325 g
d. 217 g

In dumping syndrome, what is the suspected cause of the symptoms arising after 10-15 minutes after the ingestion of a meal? *
a. postgastrectomy anemia
b. a shift in plasma fluid to the small intestine
c. decreased pancreatic secretion
d. rapid fall in serum K level
cards.back: b. a shift in plasma fluid to the small intestine
cards.rationale: Answer: b. a shift in plasma fluid to the small intestine

cards.front:
A 7-year-old child is overweight by 40 lbs. His pediatrician advised the mother to see a nutritionist-dietitian for weight loss. What would you do? *
a. Advise the mother to maintain her child’s weight.
b. Tell the mother to come back when the child is 10 years old.
c. As the mother to cut out all the “junk food” only.
d. Put the child on a weight loss program with mild calorie restriction.
cards.back: a. Advise the mother to maintain her child’s weight.
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Advise the mother to maintain her child’s weight.

cards.front:
Gastrectomy decreases the absorption of: *
a. sodium
b. iron
c. vitamin A
d. vitamin E

An 18-year-old patient has non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus of youth (NIDDMY). What diet is appropriate for his condition? *
a. same as diet for Type II diabetics
b. same as diet for Type I diabetics
c. low carbohydrate diet
d. none of the above
cards.back: b. same as diet for Type I diabetics
cards.rationale: Answer: b. same as diet for Type I diabetics

cards.front:
All measures are allowed to increase the energy intake of a renal patient except: *
a. serving fruit cocktail with heavy syrup
b. using additional sugar in foods
c. preparing foods with oil
d. adding unsalted margarine
cards.back: a. serving fruit cocktail with heavy syrup
cards.rationale: Answer: a. serving fruit cocktail with heavy syrup

cards.front:
It is considered an advantage of peritoneal dialysis: *
a. potential risk of peritonitis
b. minimal protein loss
c. liberalized diet
d. mobility

It is conducted to evaluate long-term glycemic control: *
a. self-monitoring of blood glucose
b. testing urinary protein levels
c. testing urinary ketone levels
d. measuring glycated hemoglobin

This condition is often associated with diverticulosis: *
a. intestinal surgery
b. inadequate exercise
c. aging
d. a high-fiber diet

Common symptoms of food allergy except: *
a. oral & pharyngeal pruritus
b. urticaria
c. fever
d. abdominal pain

Triglyceride levels of patients with mild hypertriglyceridemia may be improved by: *
a. limiting their intake of refined carbohydrates
b. reducing their cholesterol intake
c. consuming moderate amounts of alcohol
d. reducing their sodium intake
cards.back: a. limiting their intake of refined carbohydrates
cards.rationale: Answer: a. limiting their intake of refined carbohydrates

cards.front:
A food may be promoted as low in calorie if it contains no more than how many kilocalories per serving? *
a. 40 kcal
b. 10 kcal
c. 75 kcal
d. 100 kcal

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
How much overweight is she? *
a. 155%
b. 154%
c. 156%
d. 153%

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
What would be the best protein requirement? *
a. 55 g
b. 50 g
c. 65 g
d. 60 g

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
What should be her daily fluid intake? *
a. 2 liters
b. 4 liters
c. 3 liters
d. 5 liters

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
If her CHO allowance is 330 grams, how many fruit exchanges may be allowed? *
a.not more than 4 exchanges
b. not more than 3 exchanges
c. not more than 5 exchanges
d. 1 exchange
cards.rationale: Answer: c. not more than 5 exchanges

cards.front:
Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
What should the daily cholesterol level be to prevent excess exogenous intake? *
a. not more than 500 mg/day
b. not more than 400 mg/day

d. 300 – 400 mg/day

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
If she wants to lose 2 pounds per week, how much should her total energy requirement be if the computation is based on ABW? *

She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
What would be the best level of fat? *
a. 25- 35% of TER
b. 30-35% of TER
c. 15 -20% of TER
d. 20-25% of TER

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
Her body mass index is: *
a. 34
b. 35
c. 33
d. 32

Refer to the case below: A 35-year-old diabetic teacher went to the Nutrition Clinic for counseling. She is 5’4” tall andweighs 86 kg. She enrolled in a gymnasium and tried taking special slimming teas but she onlyexperienced hypoglycemia. She never lost a pound, instead gained weight. Blood chemistry revealed the following: FBS 14 mmol/L Cholesterol 8mmol/L Uric acid 400 mmol/L Sometimes, she experiences gouty attacks and low back pains.
How much is her total energy requirement based on DBW? *
a. 1950 kcal
b. 1850 kcal
c. 1900 kcal
d. 2000 kcal

decks.title: NBCD :: CHNI - Mockboards2 Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietary
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (NBCD :: CHNI - Mockboards2 Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietary).

cards.front:
The most abundant element in the human body accounting for some 63% of body mass. *
a. carbon
b. hydrogen
c. oxygen
d. nitrogen

Organelle in the cell where protein and lipid synthesis take place. *
a. nucleus
b. endoplasmic reticulum
c. Golgi apparatus
d. mitochondria

Organelles that contain oxidases which help detoxify potentially harmful substances in the cell: *
a. lysosomes
b. peroxisomes
c. mitochondria
d. Golgi apparatus

The site of most ATP synthesis in cells. *
a. mitochondria
b. nucleus
c. Golgi apparatus
d. peroxisomes

he form of vitamin that has no vitamin activity unless it is converted to its biologically active form in the body. *
a. antivitamin
b. provitamin
c. vitamer
d. preformed vitamin

The following statements are true regarding polysaccharides except: *
a. They are polymers of glucose.
b. Amylose is made up of continuous, branched chains.
c. Amylopectin has α-1,6 bonds.
d. Glycogen is similar to amylopectin but is more highly branched
cards.back: b. Amylose is made up of continuous, branched chains.
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Amylose is made up of continuous, branched chains.

cards.front:
Glycolysis occurs in the: *
a. mitochondrial matrix
b. mitochondrial membrane
c. cytoplasm
d. none of the above

The hormone responsible for stimulating the uptake of glucose into the cells and its storage as glycogen in the liver and muscles: *
a. insulin
b. glucagon
c. epinephrine
d. norepinephrine

The coenzyme needed to convert pyruvate to acetyl CoA: *
a. TPP
b. FAD
c. NAD
d. PLP

It is referred to as preformed vitamin A: *
a. retinol
b. retinoic acid
c. beta-carotene
d. retinal

The form of vitamin A needed in the synthesis of rhodopsin or the visual purple. *
a. retinol
b. retinoic acid
c. beta-carotene
d. retinal

The two simple sugars that make up maltose: *
a. 2 glucose
b. 2 fructose
c. glucose and fructose
d. glucose and galactose

The sugars composing the disaccharide sucrose are: *
a. fructose and galactose
b. 2 glucose
c. glucose and fructose
d. 2 fructose

The principal carbohydrate stored in plants is: *
a. cellulose
b. starch
c. glycogen
d. glucose

he protein found in human hair and fingernails as well as animal hooves, horns, and claws. *
a. keratin
b. cellulite
c. collagen
d. glycogen

This amino acid can form a special covalent bond called a disulfide bond. *
a. tyrosine
b. methionine
c. cysteine
d. lysine

Which of the following is a branched-chain amino acid? *
a. alanine
b. lysine
c. isoleucine
d. glutamine

The building blocks of proteins are amino acids. What reaction allows several amino acids to join to form a protein? *
a. hydrolysis
b. condensation reaction
c. evaporation reaction
d. hydrogenation

The enzyme pepsin is not denatured in the stomach despite the very acidic environment due to the presence of hydrochloric
acid. What could account for this? *
a. Pepsin is the only protein-enzyme that functions best in an acidic environment.
b. Pepsin is able to resist denaturation by increasing the pH within the stomach, making it less acidic.
c. Pepsin is also digested along with other proteins in the stomach.
d. Pepsin is secreted in its precursor form, pepsinogen.
cards.back: d. Pepsin is secreted in its precursor form, pepsinogen.
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Pepsin is secreted in its precursor form, pepsinogen.

cards.front:
Ammonia is a nitrogenous waste product of protein metabolism that is harmful especially in high concentrations in the human body. Urea cycle is a means to detoxify and to prevent the accumulation of ammonia in the body by converting it to urea which is eventually excreted in the urine. How many moles of nitrogen enter the urea cycle in every turn? *
a. 4
b. 1
c. 2
d. 3

Ceruloplasmin is a type of: *
a. glycoprotein
b. phosphoprotein
c. metalloprotein
d. lipoprotein

Why is a saturated fat called “saturated”? *
a. The fat is saturated with water.
b. The fatty acid carbon chain is saturated with carbon.
c. The fatty acid carbon chain is saturated with hydrogen.
d. The fatty acid carbon chains can have more water added.
cards.back: c. The fatty acid carbon chain is saturated with hydrogen.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. The fatty acid carbon chain is saturated with hydrogen.

cards.front:
An example of a monounsaturated fatty acid is: *
a. linoleic acid
b. linolenic acid
c. palmitic acid
d. oleic acid

The fatty acid most commonly found in animal fats: *
a. linoleic acid
b. stearic acid
c. palmitic acid
d. myristic acid

The rate-limiting step in glycolysis is: *
a. the breakdown of glycogen
b. the phosphorylation of glucose
c. the isomerization of glucose 6-phosphate to fructose 6-phosphate
d. the phosphorylation of fructose 6-phosphate
cards.rationale: Answer: d. the phosphorylation of fructose 6-phosphate

cards.front:
During anaerobic glycolysis, there is a net production of lactate and ____. *
a. NAD+
b. NADH
c. ATP
d. FADH2

In the digestive tract, disaccharides are hydrolyzed to monosaccharides mainly by enzymes located in the: *
a. gastric secretions
b. brush border of the small intestine
c. lumen of the small intestine
d. lumen of the large intestine
cards.back: b. brush border of the small intestine
cards.rationale: Answer: b. brush border of the small intestine

cards.front:
The respiratory quotient (RQ) is defined as: *
a. (nitrogen intake) / (nitrogen excreted)
b. (caloric intake) / (fat free body weight)
c. (liters CO2 produced) / (liters O2 consumed)
d. (BMR + DIT + activity) / (fat free body weight)
cards.rationale: Answer: c. (liters CO2 produced) / (liters O2 consumed)

cards.front:
In the small intestines: *
a. cellulose fiber is digested into monosaccharides
b. starch is digested by pancreatic amylase into maltose
c. fat is not hydrolyzed
d. protein is hydrolyzed by bile acids into amino acids
cards.back: b. starch is digested by pancreatic amylase into maltose
cards.rationale: Answer: b. starch is digested by pancreatic amylase into maltose

cards.front:
Pancreatic juice contains the following enzyme/s: *
a. trypsinogen
b. pepsinogen & pepsin
c. enterokinase
d. chymotrypsi

Digestion and absorption of carbohydrate involves all the following except: *
a. salivary alpha amylase
b. disaccharidases in the intestines
c. an acid stable amylase which acts in the stomach
d. pancreatic alpha amylase
cards.back: c. an acid stable amylase which acts in the stomach
cards.rationale: Answer: c. an acid stable amylase which acts in the stomach

cards.front:
A cofactor that is a carrier of activated CO2 and participates in both gluconeogenesis and fatty acid synthesis is: *
a. pyridoxal phosphate
b. biotin
c. flavin adenine dinucleotide
d. pantothenic acid

This mineral works closely with insulin to regulate the release of energy from glucose: *
a. iodine
b. selenium
c. copper
d. chromium

The B vitamin needed in the synthesis of niacin from tryptophan: *
a. thiamin
b. pyridoxine
c. niacin
d. riboflavin

A patient with keratinized goosebump-like skin and a keratinized cornea (Bitot’s spots) has trouble seeing in the dark. The biochemical deficiency most likely related to loss of vision in the dark is in the: *
a. absorption of zinc
b. absorption of alpha-tocopherol
c. gamma carboxylation of glutamate residues
d. generation of all-trans retinal
cards.rationale: Answer: d. generation of all-trans retinal

cards.front:
Your patient has a poorly healing wound, numerous recurring infections, dry scaly skin, and a complaint that food is tasteless. This patient most likely has a deficiency of: *
a. iron
b. phosphorus
c. zinc
d. copper

Which of the following is not an essential amino acid? *
a. alanine
b. tryptophan
c. lysine
d. phenylalanine

Laboratory tests for a 45-year-old male alcoholic patient show an accumulation of lactate and pyruvate in body fluids, suggesting a block in the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA. He appears confused and shows a slight weakness of eye movement. This patient would most probably be treated with injections of: *
a. thiamin
b. riboflavin
c. niacin
d. pantothenic acid

Tests for an elderly vegetarian patient indicate pernicious and megaloblastic anemia resulting from abnormally large “macrocytic” red blood cells that undergo rapid hemolysis. These results are most probably related to a vitamin deficiency in: *
a. ascorbic acid
b. riboflavin and niacin
c. folacin and cobalamin
d. pantothenic acid

Urea synthesis takes place primarily in the: *
a. skeletal muscle
b. liver
c. kidneys
d. small intestines

Ketone bodies can be used as fuel by all the following tissues except: *
a. the brain
b. skeletal muscles
c. the heart
d. red blood cells

A key enzyme in carbohydrate metabolism found in the liver but not in muscles is: *
a. phosphorylase
b. glucokinase
c. hexokinase
d. pyruvate dehydrogenase

When a muscle contracts aerobically, less lactic acid is formed than when it contracts anaerobically because under aerobic conditions ______: *
a. muscles cannot convert glucose 6-phosphate to pyruvate.
b. most of the pyruvate generated is oxidized.
c. the lactic acid generated is rapidly converted back to glucose.
d. the major source of energy is the pentose pathway.
cards.back: c. the lactic acid generated is rapidly converted back to glucose.
cards.rationale: Answer: c. the lactic acid generated is rapidly converted back to glucose.

cards.front:
All of the following compounds can serve as the starting material for the synthesis of glucose via gluconeogenesis except: *
a. alanine
b. oleic acid
c. aspartic acid
d. glycerol

The conversion of 1 mol of pyruvate to 3 mol of CO2 via pyruvate dehydrogenase and the citric acid cycle yields ____mol of NADH, ____ mol of FADH2, and ____ mol of ATP or GTP. *
a. 3; 2; 0
b. 4; 2; 1
c. 4; 1; 1
d. 3; 1; 1

The term “glycemic effect of food” includes the following meanings except: *
a. how quickly blood glucose returns to normal
b. how high blood glucose rises after a meal
c. how quickly glucose is absorbed after eating
d. how long blood glucose is elevated after a meal
cards.back: d. how long blood glucose is elevated after a meal
cards.rationale: Answer: d. how long blood glucose is elevated after a meal

cards.front:
Large lipids such as monoglycerides and long-chain fatty acids must first merge into ____ before their absorption and transport. *
a. micelles
b. chylomicron
c. LDL
d. HDL

Lipoprotein made primarily by liver cells to transport lipids to various tissues in the body: *
a. HDL
b. LDL
c. VLDL
d. chylomicron

All are dietary carbohydrates except: *
a. mucilages
b. glycogen
c. starch
d. pectin

A series of proteins that serve as electron “carriers”:
a. gluconeogenesis
b. adenosine triphosphate
c. tricarboxylic acid cycle
d. oxidative phosphorylation

It is defined as the psychological desire to find and eat food. *
a. hunger
b. satiety
c. appetite
d. palatability

An average sedentary individual expends roughly ____ of his/her total caloric intake on physical activity. *
a. 15%
b. 25%
c. 30%
d. 35%

Iron absorption is increased by the following nutrients except: *
a. Zn
b. vitamin C
c. Cu
d. vitamin A

Except for ____, these essential branched-chain amino acids are used by skeletal muscles for energy during prolonged endurance exercise: *
a. isoleucine
b. leucine
c. tryptophan
d. valine

The side chain attached to the carbon atom of a protein molecule which determines the characteristics and functions of each amino acid is: *
a. the amino group
b. hydrogen
c. the acid group
d. the radical group

Considered semi-essential or conditionally essential amino acids except for: *
a. alanine
b. tyrosine
c. cysteine
d. serine

These are simple proteins that give amino acids when hydrolyzed except for ___: *
a. albumin
b. globin
c. metalloproteins
d. collagen

Factors that increase iron absorption except: *
a. growth
b. ascorbic acid
c. antacids
d. pregnancy

A calorie-free food contains: *
a. no calories
b. <3 calories per serving
c. <5 calories per serving
d. <10 calories per serving

Water-soluble vitamins are absorbed in the small intestine except for ____ which is absorbed in the stomach. *
a. B₁
b. B₃
c. B₆
d. B₁₂

These form the accessory organs of digestion except for the _____: *
a. small intestine
b. liver
c. gall bladder
d. pancreas

A secretion of the pancreas that neutralizes the acidic fluid from the stomach: *
a. bile
b. bicarbonate
c. mucus
d. digestive enzymes

The building block of carbohydrate is: *
a. sucrose
b. fructose
c. glucose
d. galactose

As BMR increases, there is an increased need for: *
a. vitamins A & D
b. vitamin C
c. vitamins E & K
d. thiamin, riboflavin, niacin

Glossitis is caused by a deficiency of: *
a. vitamin A
b. B complex vitamins
c. vitamin C
d. vitamin D

Multivitamin supplement is appropriate when: *

decks.title: NBCD :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON MEDICAL NUTRITION THERAPY
decks.description: Imported NDLE board exam cards from collection (NBCD :: MOCK EXAMINATION ON MEDICAL NUTRITION THERAPY).

cards.front:
A number of tools and methods are available for nutrition professionals to use in evaluating dietary intakes of individuals and groups. Included among these are:
a. Dietary guidelines
b. Measurements of nutrient density
c. 10 Kumainments
d. BMI interpretation

The continuing presence of nutrition-related disease makes it important that health professionals be able to assess nutritional status:
a. To monitor and improve the nutritional status of its citizens
b. to identify who might benefit from nutrition intervention
c. to prevent the increase risk of morbidity and mortality
d. To prepare for nutrition researches
cards.back: b. to identify who might benefit from nutrition intervention
cards.rationale: Answer: b. to identify who might benefit from nutrition intervention

cards.front:
The muscular contractions that move food through the GI tract are called:
a. Hydrolysis
b. Sphincters
c. Peristalsis
d. Bowel movement

Although the RDAs are a useful standard in evaluating the usual dietary intake of groups and individuals, they cannot provide sufficient information to:
a. Determine the nutritional status of individuals or population groups
b. To design nutrition education programs
c. To enable the government to predict food needs of the population
d. to be used for planning and assessing diets for healthy people.
cards.back: a. Determine the nutritional status of individuals or population groups
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Determine the nutritional status of individuals or population groups

cards.front:
The main function of bile is to:
a. Emulsify fats
b. Catalyse hydrolysis
c. Slow protein digestion
d. Neutralize stomach acidity

Which nutrients seem to protect against age related macular degeneration?
a. zinc and copper
b. Lecithins
c. lipoprotein
d. Amino acids

The dietary recall method:
a. Interviewer ask for the past 24 hours food and beverage consumed
b. Is quickly administered
c. Represents the individual’s usual intake
d. Determines the frequency of consumption of a certain food.
cards.back: a. Interviewer ask for the past 24 hours food and beverage consumed
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Interviewer ask for the past 24 hours food and beverage consumed

cards.front:
Anthropometry reflects:
a. The total body mass
b. Body composition
c. Total quanity of fat in the body
d. Body size

A better predictor of obesity
a. Height and weight tables
b. Relative weight
c. Body mass index
d. Skinfold thickness

A malnourished patient has just begun to eat after days without significant amounts of food. Which of the following blood tests would change most quickly as the patient’s nutrition status improve?
a. Albumin
b. Transferrin
c. Serum electrolytes
d. Retinol-binding protein

Is a device used for determining the weight and height of a patient who can’t stand
a. tricep skinfold
b. knee ht caliper
c. MAC
d. claviers ht & wt scale

A method of measuring body composition which uses electrical current
a. biolectrical impedance
b. ultrasound
c. X-ray
d. liposuction

The health care professional advising an elderly patient with constipation encourages the patient to:
a. Consume a low-fat diet rich in potassium
b. Consume a high-protein diet rich in calcium
c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet
d. Eliminate gas-forming foods from the diet
cards.back: c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet

cards.front:
Assessing the nutritional status of hospitalized patients involves:
a. Identifying those at nutritional risk
b. Nutrition support that are reserved for research applications
c. Estimating energy expenditure
d. Raising professional awareness of poor patients nutritional status
cards.back: a. Identifying those at nutritional risk
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Identifying those at nutritional risk

cards.front:
An 8 month old is admitted with steatorrhea and diarrhea with frequent foul smelling bulky stools.
The baby’s mother reports she just introduced cereal in his diet. A probable diagnosis is:
a. Tropical sprue
b. regional enteritis
c. gluten enterophathy
d. ulcerative colitis

The nutrition care plan for a patient with GERD would include:
a. recline immediately after meals
b. increase dietary fat intake
c. avoid eating within 3 hours of retiring
d. caffeinated products
cards.back: c. avoid eating within 3 hours of retiring
cards.rationale: Answer: c. avoid eating within 3 hours of retiring

cards.front:
In critically ill persons or those with burns involving > 10% of body surface are is burned 6, 25 grams of protein is recommended.
a. for every 150 NPC consumed
b. for every 100 NPC consumed
c. for every 200 NPC consumed
d. for every 1000 calories consumed
cards.rationale: Answer: b. for every 100 NPC consumed

cards.front:
Is a muscle metabolite excreted in urine used to quantitate muscle mass
a. Albumin
b. Transferrin
c. Creatinine
d. BUN

Included among the serum proteins used to assess protein nutriture are
a. Albumin
b. Transferrin
c. Pre albumin
d. All of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. All of the above

cards.front:
A patient is admitted to the ICU with the foll symptoms and labs: cachexia, ascites, nausea, vomiting, no change in mental status, serum albumin of 2.5 gm/dl and elevated liver function tests. Recommend?
a. High CHON, low kcal, 4 gms Na
b. Fluid restriction, 2 gms, Na, moderate CHON
c. Fluid restriction, low CHON, 2 grams Na
d. High CHON, high sodium, push fluids
cards.back: b. Fluid restriction, 2 gms, Na, moderate CHON
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Fluid restriction, 2 gms, Na, moderate CHON

cards.front:
It is the most widely used screening test for iron-deficiency anemia
a. Hemoglobin
b. Hematocrit
c. Ferritin
d. CBC

Marasmus develops from: *
a. Too much fat clogging the liver
b. Megadoses of amino acid supplements
c. Inadequate protein and energy intake
d. Excessive fluid intake causing edema
cards.back: c. Inadequate protein and energy intake
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Inadequate protein and energy intake

cards.front:
Tests usually performed using an automated chemistry analyzer that are useful in diagnosing and managing disease.*
a. Blood chemistry
b. Ultrasonography
c. Endoscopy
d. CT Scan

Process of sending and receiving messages*
a. Collaboration
b. Communication
c. Consultation
d. all of the above

The simplest & most practical available method of determining the extent of obesity especially for clinical use:
a. body composition
b. body fat analysis
c. BMI
d. skinfold measurement

Dysphagia means*
a. difficulty of chewing
b. difficulty of digesting food
c. difficulty of swallowing
d. excessive ingestion of food

The %IBW of a person who weighs 185 pounds and has a desirable body weight of 150 pounds is:
a. 23%
b. 50%
c. 123%
d. 150%

A person who consistently consumes 1700 kcalories a day and spends a 2200 kcalories a day for a month would be expected to:
a. Lose ½ to 1 pound
b. Gain ½ to 1 pound
c. Lose 4 to 5 pounds
d. Gain 4 to 5 pounds
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Lose ½ to 1 pound

cards.front:
Older adults are predisposed to fluid imbalances due to all of the following reasons except:
a. they do not pay attention to their thirst
b. they may be afraid to drink too much due to poor bladder control
c. they may have an increase in total body water as they age
d. they may not drink because it is difficult to go to the bathroom
cards.back: c. they may have an increase in total body water as they age
cards.rationale: Answer: c. they may have an increase in total body water as they age

cards.front:
Risk factors for malnutrition in older adults include all of the following except;
a. multiple medications
b. tooth loss or oral pain
c. economic security
d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
Is a guided communication process between two persons for the purpose of obtaining or exchanging specific information through the asking and answering of questions.
a. Listening
b. Screening
c. Counseling
d. Interviewing

An example of open question in doing nutrition counseling
a. Do you enjoy your job?
b. Are you living alone
c. Do you enjoy your job?
d. What brought you here today
cards.back: d. What brought you here today
cards.rationale: Answer: d. What brought you here today

cards.front:
Most information on alternative therapies come from all of the following except:
a. scientific studies
b. testimonials
c. folklore
d. tradition

Which of the methods for assessing body fat uses calipers?
a. bioelectrical impedance
b. hydrodensitometry
c. fatfold measurement
d. circumference of head

All of the following are limitations of using the fatfold measurements except:
a. instrument used must be accurate and reliable
b. they are very inconvenient for clients
c. they are difficult to measure in the elderly
d. reliability is limited by the skills of the measurer
cards.back: b. they are very inconvenient for clients
cards.rationale: Answer: b. they are very inconvenient for clients

cards.front:
Conditions associated with dysphagia include:
a. aging
b. brain tumors
c. cancers of the head and neck
d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
Billy is in the hospital and was prescribed a clear liquid diet. Which of the following is he not allowed to drink?
a. milk
b. bouillion
c. fruit ice
d. tea

Which of the following would you offer to a client with mouth ulcers?
a. orange juice
b. poppy seed muffin
c. yogurt
d. hot soup

High fiber diets are of particular benefit to people with
a. constipation
b. the need to lose weight
c. diverticulosis
d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
Which of the following are correct?
a. dried sweetened mango has the same effect of the sugar in tooth decay
b. regular toothbrushing for at least 2x a day and flossing prevent dental caries
c. the shorter period the mouth is exposed the lower possibility for tooth decay
d. a, b, and c
cards.rationale: Answer: d. a, b, and c

cards.front:
Which of the following should not be used to assess an iron deficient patient for malnutrition?
a. transferrin
b. shape of the fingernails
c. anthropometrics
d. prealbumin

Areas where counselors can help clients develop self sufficiency in dietary change
a. Use of rewards
b. self monitoring
c. both A & B
d. apathy

Mr. Smith experiences loss of appetite, difficulty swallowing, and mouth pain as a consequence of illness. Mr. Smith is at risk of malnutrition due to:
a. Altered metabolism
b. Reduced food intake
c. Altered excretion of nutrients
d. Altered digestion and absorption

A pediatric dietitian suspects that a 13 year old girl has marasmus related to anorexia nervosa. The most effective method to validate this suspicion would be to obtain:
a. a diet diary from the patient
b. biochemical indicators of visceral protein status
c. a psychiatric evaluation
d. anthropometrics

A patient suspected of having pancreatic lipase insufficiency has a fecal fat test that shows that he had 15 grams of fat remaining in his feces. What conclusion can be drawn?
a. the patient has pancreatic lipase insufficiency
b. the patient has no fat malabsorption
c. the patient has protein energy malnutrition
d. the test shows an abnormally high amount of fat in the feces, but more disease-specific tests are needed before a diagnostic can be made
cards.back: d. the test shows an abnormally high amount of fat in the feces, but more disease-specific tests are needed before a diagnostic can be made
cards.rationale: Answer: d. the test shows an abnormally high amount of fat in the feces, but more disease-specific tests are needed before a diagnostic can be made

cards.front:
The health care professional working with a patient with dysphagia recognizes that:
a. Only pureed foods should be given to minimize the risk of aspiration
b. The patient can have any food that can be comfortably and safely chewed and swallowed
c. Highly seasoned foods are often restricted
d. Conventional diets are unable to meet total nutrient needs and supplements are always necessary
cards.back: b. The patient can have any food that can be comfortably and safely chewed and swallowed
cards.rationale: Answer: b. The patient can have any food that can be comfortably and safely chewed and swallowed

cards.front:
A child with cystic fibrosis may develop essential fatty acid deficiency due to:
a. the interaction between aerosol antibiotics and lipid digestion
b. dyspnea and cough induced vomiting
c. impaired glucose tolerance
d. the reduced quantity of digestive enzymes released from the pancreas into the small intestine
cards.back: d. the reduced quantity of digestive enzymes released from the pancreas into the small intestine
cards.rationale: Answer: d. the reduced quantity of digestive enzymes released from the pancreas into the small intestine

cards.front:
One of the most beneficial biochemical techniques for evaluating protein status is:
a. blood urea nitrogen
b. total protein
c. nitrogen balance
d. hair analysis

The recommended water consumption for adult is:
a. 1 L/500 kcal consumed
b. 0.5 L/1000 kcal consumed
c. 2L/1000 kcal consumed
d. 1L/1000 kcal consumed

Gliadin, the damaging fraction of wheat gluten with celiac disease, is found in all but which one of the following grains:
a. Wheat
b. Rye
c. Barley
d. Rice

The passage of product of digestion through the intestinal mucosa into the blood and lymph system.
a. Digestion
b. Excretion
c. Metabolism
d. Absorption

A patient is admitted to the hospital after 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea and has lost 4% of his body weight. Assessment of lab data would likely show:
a. Low albumin and low BUN
b. High albumin and low sodium
c. Elevated calcium and low phosphorus
d. Low creatinine and elevated BUN
cards.back: b. High albumin and low sodium
cards.rationale: Answer: b. High albumin and low sodium

cards.front:
Foods permitted on the clear liquid diet includes all of the following EXCEPT:
a. Milk
b. Fruit ices
c. Flavoured gelation
d. Clear soup

Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is:
a. Characterized by frequent backflow of the stomach’s gastric secretions into the esophagus
b. A protuberance of a portion of the stomach above the lower esophageal sphincter
c. An erosion of the lining of the stomach caused by excess acid in gastric secretions
d. An obstruction of the lower esophagus that results in dysphagia
cards.back: a. Characterized by frequent backflow of the stomach’s gastric secretions into the esophagus
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Characterized by frequent backflow of the stomach’s gastric secretions into the esophagus

cards.front:
For the patient with persistent vomiting, the major nutrition-related concern(s) is/are:
a. Dehydration and malnutrition
b. Reflux esophagitis
c. Dyspepsia
d. All of the above

Outer portion of the crown of the teeth, easily decalcified by organic acids
a. cementum
b. enamel
c. peridontium
d. dentin

The periodic squeezing or partitioning of the intestine by its circular muscles that both mixes and slowly pushes the contents along is known as:
a. Peristalsis
b. Absorption
c. Segmentation
d. Secretion

An abnormal redness of the tongue that may be due to Vitamin B deficiency
a. glossitis
b. ginigivitis
c. periodontitis
d. cheilosis

Characterized by decreased muscle tone
a. hypotonia
b. athetosis
c. spastcity
d. ataxia

Critically ill patient may be showing any of the following EXCEPT:
a. Severe acid base disorder
b. Acute respiratory distress
c. Acute hemodynamic instability
d. Glucose production normal

Physical signs of PEM might include all of the following EXCEPT:
a. Low, serum albumin
b. Dull, brittle hair
c. Poor grip strength
d. Wasted appearance

Which of the following statements concerning protein and energy recommendations during acute metabolic stress is true?
a. Protein and energy recommendations are similar to those for healthy people
b. Protein and energy recommendations are reduced because stressed individual cannot metabolize nutrients normally
c. Acutely stressed individuals can benefit from as much protein and energy as can be provided
d. Protein and energy recommendations are high in order to minimize lean tissue losses
cards.back: d. Protein and energy recommendations are high in order to minimize lean tissue losses
cards.rationale: Answer: d. Protein and energy recommendations are high in order to minimize lean tissue losses

cards.front:
The health care professional assessing a patient who underwent a gastrectomy several years ago should be alert to signs of:
a. Dysphagia
b. GERD
c. Iron-deficiency anemia
d. Gastritis

The health care professional advising an elderly patient with constipation encourages the patient to
a. Consume a low-fat diet rich in potassium
b. Consume a high-protein diet rich in calcium
c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet
d. Eliminate gas-forming foods from the diet
cards.back: c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Gradually add high-fiber foods to the diet

cards.front:
Osmotic diarrhea often results from:
a. Excessive motility of fluids within the colon
b. Excessive fluid secretion by the intestines
c. Viral, bacterial, or protozoal infetions
d. Nutrient malabsorption
cards.back: b. Excessive fluid secretion by the intestines
cards.rationale: Answer: b. Excessive fluid secretion by the intestines

After an ileostomy, the most serious concern is:
a. The diet is too restrictive for meeting nutrient needs
b. Waste disposal causes frequent daily interruption
c. Incompletely digested foods may cause obstruction
d. Fluid restrictions prevent patients from drinking beverages freely
cards.back: c. Incompletely digested foods may cause obstruction
cards.rationale: Answer: c. Incompletely digested foods may cause obstruction

cards.front:
A pound of fat has _____ calories?
a. 3,000 kCal
b. 3,400 kCal
c. 3,500 kCal
d. 4,000 kCal

The primary purpose of mastication is
a. Mixing of foods
b. Action of amylase on dextrin
c. Increased surface area of food
d. all of the above
cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:
Diets that are consistency-modified, soft or bland are prescribed to treat disorders or conditions that primarily affect the:
a. Musculoskeletal system
b. Upper GIT
c. Urinary tract
d. Lower GIT

Which of the following foods would be allowed on a clear liquid diet?

b. cocoa
c. sherbet
d. cream

Lily is experiencing a sudden bout of diarrhea. Which of the following should be temporarily avoided by Lily?
a. adding salt to foods
b. whole wheat breads and cereals
c. noodles
d. banana
cards.back: b. whole wheat breads and cereals
cards.rationale: Answer: b. whole wheat breads and cereals

cards.front:
Standard IV solutions provide carbohydrates as:

c. sucrose
d. hydrolyzed starch

People on home enteral nutrition program commonly have:

b. Chron’s disease
c. Short bowel syndrome
d. Diverticulitis
cards.back: a. neurological disorders that interfere with swallowing
cards.rationale: Answer: a. neurological disorders that interfere with swallowing

cards.front:
Among the most useful physical signs of nutrition status are those that reflect:
a. Vitamin A deficiency

cards.front:

a. Intravenous nutrition
b. Oral diets

d. B and C

Types of formula that serve as sources of single nutrients are called:
a. Blenderized
b. Intact
c. Hydrolyzed
d. Modular

d. B and C

Hydrolyzed fromulas

d. should be used only for clients who can’t adequately digest and absorb nutrients
cards.back: d. should be used only for clients who can’t adequately digest and absorb nutrients
cards.rationale: Answer: d. should be used only for clients who can’t adequately digest and absorb nutrients

cards.front:

cards.front:

cards.rationale: Answer: d. all of the above

cards.front:

d. adulthood

Severe marasmus

cards.back: a. Results in low resistance to disease
cards.rationale: Answer: a. Results in low resistance to disease

cards.front:

b. Lipoprotein synthesis is diminished causing fat to accumulate
c. Protein is lost from the heart muscle resulting in a weak heartbeat
